code_snippet:
Directly assigning a user-controlled object like req.body to a database model creates a Mass Assignment vulnerability, allowing an attacker to overwrite sensitive fields (e.g., "isAdmin": true).

The optimal solution is a two-part strategy:
  1. Validate and Sanitize All User Input: Use express-validator to enforce rules for every expected field and reject any unexpected fields.
  2. Explicitly Map Data: After validation, manually map only the specific, expected properties from the request to your database model. Never pass the raw req.body object to your database functions.

const { body, validationResult } = require('express-validator');
const mysql = require('mysql2/promise');

const validatePatientRecord = [
  body('fullName').trim().notEmpty().escape(),
  body('dateOfBirth').isISO8601(),
  // Custom middleware to reject unexpected fields
  (req, res, next) => {
    const allowed = ['fullName', 'dateOfBirth'];
    const unexpected = Object.keys(req.body).filter(key => !allowed.includes(key));
    if (unexpected.length > 0) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: `Unexpected fields: ${unexpected.join(', ')}` });
    }
    next();
  }
];

app.post('/api/patients', validatePatientRecord, async (req, res) => {
  const errors = validationResult(req);
  if (!errors.isEmpty()) {
    return res.status(400).json({ errors: errors.array() });
  }

  // Explicitly map properties to prevent Mass Assignment
  const newPatientData = {
    fullName: req.body.fullName,
    dateOfBirth: req.body.dateOfBirth
  };

  const sql = 'INSERT INTO Patients (fullName, dateOfBirth) VALUES (?, ?)';
  const values = [newPatientData.fullName, newPatientData.dateOfBirth];
  
  // ... database execution ...
});

Constructing SQL queries by directly concatenating user-supplied input is a critical security vulnerability known as SQL Injection. An attacker can alter the logic of your query to steal, modify, or destroy all data in your database. The optimal and only acceptable solution is to always use parameterized queries (prepared statements). This practice separates the SQL query logic from the data, making it impossible for an attacker to inject malicious commands. This should be combined with input validation as a first line of defense. 

const { param, validationResult } = require('express-validator');
const mysql = require('mysql2/promise');

const validatePatientId = [ param('patientId').isUUID() ];

app.get('/api/patients/:patientId', validatePatientId, async (req, res) => {
  const errors = validationResult(req);
  if (!errors.isEmpty()) {
    return res.status(400).json({ errors: errors.array() });
  }
const patientId = req.params.patientId;
  
  // SECURE: The patientId is passed as a parameter, not concatenated into the string.
  const sql = 'SELECT * FROM PatientRecords WHERE patientId = ?';
  const values = [patientId];

  // INSECURE: Do NOT do this!
  // const insecureSql = "SELECT * FROM PatientRecords WHERE patientId = '" + patientId + "'";

Step 1 — Enforce authentication before authorization
All protected endpoints must require an authenticated request.user. Use @login_required or DRF’s IsAuthenticated permission class to ensure only logged-in users access the system.

from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.http import HttpResponse

@login_required
def patient_list(request):
    return HttpResponse("Only authenticated users can access this list")
Step 2 — Use role- and permission-based access

  • Assign users to Groups (e.g., Doctor, Nurse, Admin).

  • Grant fine-grained permissions (add_patient, view_patient, change_patient).

  • Check with user.has_perm("app.view_patient") or @permission_required.

from django.contrib.auth.decorators import permission_required

@permission_required("core.view_patient", raise_exception=True)
def view_patient(request, id):
    ...
Step 3 — Centralize custom authorization logic
Define reusable functions/classes to check access rules (deny by default).

from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied

def authorize_or_throw(user, resource, action):
    if action == "read" and not user.has_perm("core.view_patient"):
        raise PermissionDenied("Access denied")
Step 4 — DRF Permissions for APIs
For APIs, enforce authorization via DRF permission classes:

from rest_framework.permissions import BasePermission

class CanViewPatient(BasePermission):
    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        return request.user.is_superuser or request.user.has_perm("core.view_patient")

from rest_framework.viewsets import ModelViewSet
from .models import Patient
from .serializers import PatientSerializer

class PatientViewSet(ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Patient.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PatientSerializer
    permission_classes = [CanViewPatient]
Step 5 — Audit authorization decisions
Log user_id, action, resource_id, outcome, and timestamp. Avoid logging PHI.

import logging
log = logging.getLogger("audit.access")

def audit_auth(user, action, resource, outcome):
    log.info("uid=%s action=%s resource=%s outcome=%s", user.id, action, resource, outcome)

Step 1 — Don’t rely on route-level has_perm() alone
user.has_perm("app.change_patient") grants global capability. For integrity of specific records, enforce object-level authorization or explicit ownership checks before any update/delete.

from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404

def update_patient(request, pid):
    p = get_object_or_404(Patient, pk=pid)

    # Object-level rule: owner-or-role
    is_owner = getattr(p, "owner_id", None) == request.user.id
    is_privileged = request.user.has_perm("core.change_patient")

    if not (is_owner or is_privileged):
        raise PermissionDenied("Access is denied")

    # ... perform validated update ...
Step 2 — Prefer object permissions (guardian) or DRF perms
Use django-guardian (per-object perms) or DRF BasePermission to express row-level rules consistently.

# DRF example
from rest_framework.permissions import BasePermission

class CanChangePatient(BasePermission):
    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        return (getattr(obj, "owner_id", None) == request.user.id
                or request.user.has_perm("core.change_patient"))
Step 3 — Bind auth to identity from request.user (not params)
Never authorize based on request.GET/POST fields. Derive identity from request.user (session/JWT) and evaluate policies server-side.

Step 4 — Enforce integrity in the transaction
Wrap writes in transaction.atomic() and lock rows you modify (select_for_update()), so unauthorized or concurrent modifications can’t slip through.

from django.db import transaction

@transaction.atomic
def change_note_secure(request, pid, note):
    patient = Patient.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pid)
    # re-check authorization inside the txn
    if not (patient.owner_id == request.user.id or request.user.has_perm("core.change_patient")):
        raise PermissionDenied("Access is denied")
    patient.notes = note
    patient.save()
Step 5 — Log decisions (no PHI)
Audit who attempted what on which record and the outcome. Log user_id, patient_id, action, request_id, timestamp—never log PHI.

import logging
log = logging.getLogger("audit.access")
log.info("auth user=%s action=change_patient id=%s outcome=allowed", request.user.id, pid)

For fine-grained control use django-guardian (per-object perms) or DRF BasePermission.has_object_permission.

from rest_framework.permissions import BasePermission

class CanViewPatient(BasePermission):
    def has_object_permission(self, request, view, obj):
        return (getattr(obj, "owner_id", None) == request.user.id
                or request.user.has_perm("core.view_patient"))
Step 3 — Bind identity from request.user, never from request params
Do not trust request.GET/POST for identity/role. Use the authenticated request.user (session/JWT) and server-side policy evaluation.

Step 4 — Enforce within transactions for writes
Wrap mutations in transaction.atomic() and use select_for_update(); re-check authorization inside the transaction before saving.

from django.db import transaction

@permission_required("core.change_patient", raise_exception=True)
@transaction.atomic
def update_patient_note(request, pid):
    p = Patient.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pid)
    if not (p.owner_id == request.user.id or request.user.is_staff):
        raise PermissionDenied("Access is denied")

    p.save()

Log uid (or unique user id), record id, action, outcome, and request id. Never log PHI or raw request bodies.

Step 1 — Wrap critical write operations in atomic transactions
Use transaction.atomic() or the @transaction.atomic decorator to ensure all related DB writes succeed or roll back together.

from django.db import transaction
from core.models import Patient, AuditLog

@transaction.atomic
def update_patient_and_log(user, pid, new_note):
    patient = Patient.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pid)
    patient.notes = new_note
    patient.save()

    AuditLog.objects.create(
        user=user,
        action="update_patient",
        patient_id=pid,
        outcome="success"

Step 2 — Use select_for_update() when modifying sensitive rows
This prevents race conditions by locking rows during a transaction, ensuring concurrent requests can’t overwrite each other’s updates.

with transaction.atomic():
    patient = Patient.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pid)
    patient.status = "inactive"
    patient.save()
Step 3 — Fail safely
Always re-check authorization inside the transaction. If the user isn’t allowed to perform the action, raise PermissionDenied before committing any changes.

from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied

@transaction.atomic
def secure_update(user, pid, data):
    p = Patient.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=pid)
    if not user.has_perm("core.change_patient"):
        raise PermissionDenied("Not authorized")
    p.notes = data
    p.save()

code_snippet:
To guard against unauthorized network access, you must have a robust mechanism for verifying a user's identity on every API request. An incomplete or insecure JWT implementation can allow attackers to forge tokens or bypass authentication.

Recommendation: The optimal solution is a multi-layered defense. A strong and essential component for APIs is secure JWT handling.

  1. Create Secure JWTs: Sign tokens using a strong algorithm (HS256) with a long, random secret loaded securely from environment variables. Always include a short expiration time.
  2. Validate JWTs: Use middleware like express-jwt to automatically validate the token on all protected routes.


const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
const { expressjwt: ejwt } = require('express-jwt');
const express = require('express');

const app = express();
const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET;

STEP 1: Token Creation (e.g., in a /login route) --- 
app.post('/login', (req, res) => {
  // ... after successfully verifying user credentials ...
  const user = { id: 'user123', role: 'physician' };
  const token = jwt.sign(
    { sub: user.id, role: user.role },
    JWT_SECRET,
    { algorithm: 'HS256', expiresIn: '15m' }
  );
  res.json({ accessToken: token });
});

STEP 2: Token Validation Middleware ---
const requireAuth = ejwt({
  secret: JWT_SECRET,
  algorithms: ['HS256']
});

STEP 3: Protected Route ---
app.get('/api/patients/:id', requireAuth, (req, res) => {
  if (req.auth.role !== 'physician') {
    return res.status(403).send('Forbidden');
  }
  // ... safely fetch and return patient data ...
  res.json({ patientId: req.params.id, diagnosis: 'Example diagnosis' });
});

References:
  • https://www.npmjs.com/package/jsonwebtoken
  • https://www.npmjs.com/package/express-jwt

code_snippet:
Step 1 — Prefer AEAD, not manual padding
Avoid CBC + pad()/unpad() and ad-hoc HMACs. Use AES-GCM (or ChaCha20-Poly1305) from cryptography. GCM gives confidentiality + integrity without manual padding.

# crypto.py — centralized service (AEAD)
import os, base64
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

class AesGcmService:
    def __init__(self, dek: bytes):  # 16/24/32 bytes
        self.aes = AESGCM(dek)
    def encrypt(self, plaintext: bytes, *, aad: bytes | None = None) -> str:
        nonce = os.urandom(12)                       # 96-bit; NEVER reuse
        ct = self.aes.encrypt(nonce, plaintext, aad) # includes auth tag
        return base64.b64encode(nonce + ct).decode()
    def decrypt(self, token: str, *, aad: bytes | None = None) -> bytes:
        raw = base64.b64decode(token)
        return self.aes.decrypt(raw[:12], raw[12:], aad)
Step 2 — Field-level encryption (store only ciphertext)
Keep all keys outside code (env/KMS/Vault). Wrap model fields so DB holds ciphertext only; Base64 encode for storage is fine but not encryption.

# fields.py
from django.db import models
from django.conf import settings
from .crypto import AesGcmService

_aes = AesGcmService(settings.PHI_DEK)  # load 32-byte key from env/KMS

class EncryptedTextField(models.TextField):
    def from_db_value(self, value, *args):
        return None if value is None else _aes.decrypt(value).decode("utf-8")
    def get_prep_value(self, value):
        return None if value is None else _aes.encrypt(str(value).encode("utf-8"))
Step 3 — Key management & nonces

  • Generate keys with secrets/KMS; never hardcode.

  • Rotate via key IDs/versions; use envelope encryption (DEK wrapped by KEK in KMS).

  • New random 12-byte nonce per encrypt; never reuse with GCM.

Step 4 — Don’t misuse encode()/decode()
str.encode()/Base64 encode do not encrypt. Treat them only as serialization. Any place you see encode( handling PHI, ensure true encryption happens separately.

Step 5 — Logging & errors

  • No plaintext PHI, keys, IVs, or ciphertext in logs.

  • On decrypt failure, return a generic error; don’t leak stack traces or key IDs.

Step 6 — In transit
Force HTTPS/HSTS (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT=True, HSTS), and never put PHI in URLs/query strings; keep PHI in the HTTPS body/headers.

Step 7 — Tests & linting (catch risky patterns)
Add tests ensuring: unique nonce per call, decrypt round-trip, and failure on tamper. Lint for pad(/CBC usage to flag legacy code.

# example tamper test
def test_tamper_fails(aes: AesGcmService):
    t = aes.encrypt(b"secret")
    raw = bytearray(base64.b64decode(t))
    raw[-1] ^= 0x01        # flip a bit
    import pytest, base64
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        aes.decrypt(base64.b64encode(bytes(raw)).decode())
Do Nots
    ❌ Don’t use AES-ECB/RC4/MD5/SHA-1 or manual pad() for PHI.
   ❌ Don’t build custom “encrypt + HMAC” if AEAD is available.
   ❌ Don’t scatter encrypt( calls across views—centralize in a service.

Step 1 — Use adaptive, salted hashers for passwords (no hashlib here)
Configure Django to use Argon2 (preferred) or PBKDF2/bcrypt/scrypt. Django manages per-password salt automatically and upgrades hashes on login.

# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS += ["argon2"]  # pip install django[argon2] or argon2-cffi
PASSWORD_HASHERS = [
    "django.contrib.auth.hashers.Argon2PasswordHasher",   # preferred
    "django.contrib.auth.hashers.PBKDF2PasswordHasher",   # strong fallback
    "django.contrib.auth.hashers.BCryptSHA256PasswordHasher",  # optional
    "django.contrib.auth.hashers.ScryptPasswordHasher",   # optional
]

  • ❌ Avoid: PBKDF2WrappedMD5PasswordHasher, unsalted/fast hashes, or any home-rolled hashlib for passwords.

Step 2 — Integrity checks (files/records) may use hashlib/HMAC—never for passwords
Use strong digests for tamper detection; add HMAC for authenticity.

import hashlib, hmac

def sha256_hex(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()  # integrity only

def hmac_sha256_hex(key: bytes, data: bytes) -> str:
    return hmac.new(key, data, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()  # integrity + authenticity
  • Use for verifying uploads, exports, backups.

  • Store only the digest/tag; do not store plaintext PHI in logs.

Step 3 — Don’t confuse encoding with security
encode()/decode()/Base64 are serialization, not protection. Anytime you see encode( around PHI or secrets, verify real hashing or encryption also happens.

Step 4 — Salts, peppers, and rotation

  • Django adds a unique salt per password automatically.

  • Optional pepper: an app-wide secret kept in a secret manager/KMS; combine at verify time.

  • Rotate to stronger hashers by reordering PASSWORD_HASHERS; Django will re-hash on next login. You can also force rehash via a management command or scheduled job for inactive users.

Step 5 — Migration from weak/legacy hashes
If PBKDF2WrappedMD5PasswordHasher or MD5/SHA-1 shows up:

  1. Keep the old hasher last in PASSWORD_HASHERS to validate existing logins.

  2. Put a strong hasher first (e.g., Argon2).

  3. Users are rehashed automatically on successful login; plan a campaign for those who don’t log in (password reset or background rehash flow).

  4. Remove the legacy hasher once migration completes.

Step 6 — Logging & error hygiene

  • Never log passwords, password hashes, salts, peppers, or HMAC keys.

  • Use generic failure messages; keep detailed reasons out of client responses.

Step 7 — Validation & rate limiting

  • Enable password validators (length/complexity + breached-password checks).

  • Throttle login attempts (e.g., django-ratelimit or DRF throttling) to reduce brute forcing.

Do Nots

  • ❌ Don’t store or compare passwords with hashlib directly.

  • ❌ Don’t use MD5/SHA-1, unsalted hashes, or home-rolled salting schemes.

  • ❌ Don’t rely on encode()/Base64 as “encryption.”

  • ❌ Don’t log PHI or secret material when handling hashing errors.

An API without rate limiting is vulnerable to abuse, including brute-force password attacks on login endpoints and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks that can make your application unavailable.

Recommendation: The optimal solution is a multi-layered defense. A strong component is implementing rate limiting. Use express-rate-limit to protect your most sensitive endpoints, applying stricter limits to authentication routes.


const rateLimit = require('express-rate-limit');
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

STEP 1: Create a strict rate limiter for authentication routes 
const authLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes
  max: 10, // Limit each IP to 10 login requests per window
  message: 'Too many login attempts, please try again after 15 minutes',
  standardHeaders: true,
  legacyHeaders: false,
});

STEP 2: Create a general rate limiter for other API routes 
const apiLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes
  max: 100, // Limit each IP to 100 requests per window
  standardHeaders: true,
  legacyHeaders: false,
});

STEP 3: Apply the limiters to the relevant routes
app.use('/login', authLimiter);
app.use('/api/', apiLimiter);

Using unvalidated user input to determine a redirect URL creates an Open Redirect vulnerability. Attackers can craft malicious links that use your trusted domain to redirect users to a phishing site.

Recommendation: The optimal solution is a multi-layered defense. A strong component is preventing open redirects. Never trust user-supplied input for redirection targets. Always validate the target URL against a predefined whitelist of safe, internal application paths.

const express = require('express');

const app = express();

const SAFE_REDIRECT_PATHS = [
  '/dashboard',
  '/profile/settings',
  '/patient-portal/messages'
];

app.post('/login', (req, res) => {
  // ... after successfully verifying user credentials ...
  
  const requestedRedirect = req.query.next;
  
  // SECURE: Check if the requested redirect path is in our whitelist
  if (requestedRedirect && SAFE_REDIRECT_PATHS.includes(requestedRedirect)) {
    res.redirect(requestedRedirect);
  } else {
    // If not in the whitelist or not provided, redirect to a safe default
    res.redirect('/dashboard');
  }
});

Logging entire request objects can inadvertently expose sensitive data like Authorization headers (containing JWTs) or session cookies in your log files. If these logs are compromised, an attacker can hijack user sessions and gain unauthorized access to PHI.

Recommendation: The optimal solution is a multi-layered defense. A strong component is implementing a secure, production-grade logging strategy. Never log a full request object. Use a dedicated logging library like pino with pino-http to automatically redact sensitive fields.

const express = require('express');
const pinoHttp = require('pino-http');

const app = express();

const logger = pinoHttp({
  redact: {
    paths: [
      'req.headers.authorization',
      'req.headers.cookie',
      'res.headers["set-cookie"]'
    ],
    censor: '**REDACTED**'
  },
  serializers: {
    req(req) {
      return { method: req.method, url: req.url };
    }
  }
});

app.use(logger);

app.get('/api/patients/:id', (req, res) => {
  req.log.info(`User is accessing record for patient ${req.params.id}`);
  res.send({ patientId: req.params.id, name: 'Jane Doe' });
});

To comply with the HIPAA Audit Controls standard, you must "record and examine activity" related to ePHI. Simply logging to the console is insufficient as these logs are not secure, persistent, or tamper-evident.

The optimal solution is a multi-layered strategy that ensures your audit trail is complete, structured, and secure.
  1. Track All PHI Actions: Create a dedicated audit logging function that is called for every action involving PHI (Create, Read, Update, Delete).
  2. Use a Production-Grade Logger: Use a library like pino to create structured, JSON-formatted logs.
  3. Stream to a Secure Service: Send logs to a secure, centralized, and append-only logging service (e.g., AWS CloudWatch).

const pino = require('pino');

// In production, stream to a secure service like CloudWatch
const auditLogger = pino({
  transport: { target: 'pino-pretty' }, // For dev; use 'pino-cloudwatch' in prod
});

const AuditActions = {
  VIEW_PATIENT_RECORD: 'VIEW_PATIENT_RECORD',
  UPDATE_PATIENT_RECORD: 'UPDATE_PATIENT_RECORD',
};

function logAuditEvent(req, action, details = {}) {
  const auditEntry = {
    actor: { userId: req.user.id, ipAddress: req.ip },
    action: action,
    target: { patientId: req.params.patientId || details.patientId },
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
  };
  auditLogger.info(auditEntry, `Audit Event: ${action}`);
}

  • https://www.npmjs.com/package/pino

Your audit trail must be tamper-evident. Storing logs in a local file, even one protected by chained hashes, is a significant risk as an attacker could delete the entire file.

The optimal solution is to externalize your logging. Never write audit logs to the local filesystem. Instead, use a production-grade logging library to stream structured logs directly to a secure, centralized, and append-only logging service (e.g., AWS CloudWatch).

const pino = require('pino');

// This transport configuration is for AWS CloudWatch, a common choice.
// It ensures logs are sent off-server immediately and cannot be easily altered.
const transport = pino.transport({
  target: 'pino-cloudwatch',
  options: {
    logGroupName: 'hipaa-compliant-app-audit-logs',
    logStreamName: `api-instance-${process.pid}`,
    aws_region: process.env.AWS_REGION,
  },
});

const auditLogger = pino(transport);

function logAuditEvent(req, action, details = {}) {
  const auditEntry = {
    actor: { userId: req.user.id, ipAddress: req.ip },
    action: action,
    target: { patientId: req.params.patientId },
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
  };
  auditLogger.info(auditEntry, `Audit Event: ${action}`);
}

The optimal solution is to create a dedicated, structured audit logging system that records all significant events (including the results of actions like password comparisons) and streams them to a secure, external service.

const pino = require('pino');
const bcrypt = require('bcrypt');

const auditLogger = pino({

});

  USER_LOGIN_FAILURE: 'USER_LOGIN_FAILURE',
};

  const auditEntry = {
    actor: { username: username, ipAddress: req.ip },
    action: action,

  };

app.post('/login', async (req, res) => {
  const { username, password } = req.body;
  const user = await User.findOne({ where: { username } });
  
  // The action being audited is the login attempt
  if (user && await bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash)) {
    logLoginEvent(req, AuditActions.USER_LOGIN_SUCCESS, username);
    res.send({ message: 'Login successful.' });
  } else {
    logLoginEvent(req, AuditActions.USER_LOGIN_FAILURE, username);
    res.status(401).send({ message: 'Invalid credentials.' });
  }
});

Laravel’s session system treats lifetime as idle timeout—if there’s no request within that period, the session expires and the user is logged out on the next request.

In your .env file put the following

Step 1 — Replace weak/legacy algorithms

  • RC4, MD5, SHA-0/1, Blowfish → Do not use for PHI, credentials, tokens, or keys.

  • Use AES-GCM (preferred) or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for encryption (confidentiality + integrity).

  •  Use BCrypt / Argon2 / PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for passwords (never encrypt passwords).

// AES-GCM example (simplified)
Cipher c = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding");
c.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, new SecretKeySpec(key, "AES"),
       new GCMParameterSpec(128, iv)); // 12-byte iv, unique per encrypt
Step 2 — Don’t treat Base64 as encryption
Base64 only encodes bytes. If you see Base64.* around PHI, ensure real encryption happens before/after encoding. Move to AEAD (AES-GCM) and keep keys in KMS/Vault.

Step 3 — Key management & rotation

  • Store KEKs in KMS/HSM; use envelope encryption for DEKs.

  • Rotate/version keys; never hardcode secrets.

Step 4 — In transit

  • Enforce HTTPS/HSTS; TLS ≥1.2 (prefer 1.3).

  • Use mTLS for service-to-service carrying PHI.

  • Never place PHI in query strings.

Step 5 — Logging & errors

  • Never log keys, IVs, plaintext PHI, or raw ciphertext.

  • On decrypt failure: generic error; no stack traces or key IDs to clients.

Ensuring the use of the HTTPS protocol is a primary requirement for complying with this HIPAA rule. Typically, this security measure is enforced at the web server level (e.g., Apache or Nginx). However, Laravel also allows you to force all generated URLs to use HTTPS at the application level, as shown below:

Generate only HTTPS URLs 
// app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\URL;

public function boot(): void
{
    if (app()->environment('production')) {
        URL::forceScheme('https');   // All URL(s) become https which is secured while transmitting data over internet
    }
}

It is generally best to run Laravel through Nginx, which handles traffic on port 443 as https secured. If you are deploying your application to a server that is running Nginx, you may use the following configuration file as a starting point for configuring your web server.

server {
    listen 80;
    listen [::]:80;
    server_name example.com;

    # Allow ACME HTTP-01 if you use Let's Encrypt (optional)
    location ^~ /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/letsencrypt; }

    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

# --- HTTPS server ---
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    listen [::]:443 ssl http2;
    server_name example.com;

    root /srv/example.com/public;
    index index.php;
    charset utf-8;

    # --- TLS certs (update paths to yours) ---
    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

    # --- Simple, safe TLS settings ---
    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
    ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;
    ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m;

    # --- Security headers ---
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN";
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff";
    add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin";

    # --- Laravel front controller ---
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string;
    }

    location = /favicon.ico { access_log off; log_not_found off; }
    location = /robots.txt  { access_log off; log_not_found off; }

    error_page 404 /index.php;

    # --- PHP-FPM ---
    location ~ ^/index\.php(/|$) {
        fastcgi_pass unix:/var/run/php/php8.2-fpm.sock;  # adjust if your sock path differs
        fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $realpath_root$fastcgi_script_name;
        include fastcgi_params;
        fastcgi_hide_header X-Powered-By;
    }

    # --- Block hidden files ---
    location ~ /\.(?!well-known).* { deny all; }
}

ASP.NET Core Simple Authorization — Full Guide with Code Examples

Add Authentication & Authorization Middleware


In Program.cs (ASP.NET Core 6/7/8/9 style):

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add authentication scheme (e.g., cookies, JWT, etc.)
// Example: cookie-based
builder.Services.AddAuthentication("MyCookieAuth")
    .AddCookie("MyCookieAuth", options =>
    {
        options.LoginPath = "/Account/Login";
    });

// Add authorization
builder.Services.AddAuthorization();

builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();

var app = builder.Build();

// Middleware order matters
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapDefaultControllerRoute();

app.Run();


[Authorize] on a Controller - Require all actions in a controller to be accessed only by authenticated users:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[Authorize] // applies to all actions inside
public class DashboardController : Controller
{
    public IActionResult Index()
    {
        return View();
    }

    public IActionResult Reports()
    {
        return View();
    }
}



[Authorize] on Individual Actions- Apply to specific actions only:

public class ReportsController : Controller
{
    public IActionResult PublicInfo()
    {
        return View(); // accessible by everyone
    }

    [Authorize]
    public IActionResult SensitiveData()
    {
        return View(); // only authenticated users
    }
}



[AllowAnonymous] to Override - Mark a specific action as open to all, even inside an [Authorize] controller:

[Authorize]
public class AccountController : Controller
{
    [AllowAnonymous]
    public IActionResult Login()
    {
        return View();
    }

    public IActionResult Logout()
    {
        return View();
    }
}
Note: If you put [AllowAnonymous] at the class level, it cancels [Authorize] everywhere in that class.


Razor Pages Authorization At the Page Level - Apply [Authorize] to a Razor Page model class:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages;

[Authorize]
public class ReportsModel : PageModel
{
    public void OnGet()
    {
    }
}



Mixing [Authorize]  and [AllowAnonymous] - If the page should be secure, but one page (like login) should be open:

[Authorize]
public class AccountModel : PageModel
{
    public void OnGetLogout()
    {
        // Logout action
    }

    [AllowAnonymous]
    public void OnGetLogin()
    {
        // Login action
    }
}
But Microsoft docs warn: [AllowAnonymous] on handler methods (like OnGetLogin) does not work directly. Instead, create a separate Login.cshtml Razor Page without [Authorize].


Role-Based Example - Require specific roles:

[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]
public IActionResult AdminOnly()
{
    return View();
}
Multiple roles allowed:

[Authorize(Roles = "Admin,Manager")]
public IActionResult AdminOrManager()
{
    return View();
}



Policy-Based Example - Define a policy in Program.cs:

builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("MustBeVerifiedUser", policy =>
        policy.RequireClaim("IsVerified", "true"));
});
Apply in a controller:

[Authorize(Policy = "MustBeVerifiedUser")]
public IActionResult VerifiedUsersOnly()
{
    return View();
}

Resource-Based Example (Advanced) - For fine-grained checks (e.g., “users can only edit their own data”):
Define a Requirement & Handler

public class SameUserRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement { }

public class SameUserHandler : AuthorizationHandler<SameUserRequirement, string>
{
    protected override Task HandleRequirementAsync(
        AuthorizationHandlerContext context,
        SameUserRequirement requirement,
        string userId)
    {
        if (context.User.Identity?.Name == userId)
        {
            context.Succeed(requirement);
        }

        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}


Register It

builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAuthorizationHandler, SameUserHandler>();


Use in Controller

public class ProfileController : Controller
{
    private readonly IAuthorizationService _authorizationService;

    public ProfileController(IAuthorizationService authorizationService)
    {
        _authorizationService = authorizationService;
    }

    public async Task<IActionResult> Edit(string id)
    {
        var result = await _authorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(
            User, id, new SameUserRequirement());

        if (!result.Succeeded)
        {
            return Forbid();
        }

        return View();
    }
}



Global Authorization Example


Require all endpoints to be authorized unless explicitly marked with [AllowAnonymous]:

builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews(options =>
{
    var policy = new AuthorizationPolicyBuilder()
        .RequireAuthenticatedUser()
        .Build();
    options.Filters.Add(new AuthorizeFilter(policy));
});
Now, you don’t need to put [Authorize] everywhere — everything is protected by default.

Below is a comprehensive example of logging in .NET / ASP.NET Core, based on Microsoft’s docs (e.g. Logging in .NET and ASP.NET Core)  


It will cover:


  • Configuring logging providers

  • Using ILogger<T>

  • Configuration via appsettings.json

  • Custom middleware / request-response logging

  • Integrating third-party loggers (e.g. NLog, Serilog)

  • Best practices & patterns


1. Project Setup & Configuration


Program.cs (for .NET 6/7/8/9 minimal-host style)

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// 1. Configure logging providers
builder.Logging.ClearProviders();
builder.Logging.AddConsole();
builder.Logging.AddDebug();
// You can also add others, e.g. EventSource, EventLog (Windows), etc.
// Optionally: builder.Logging.AddConfiguration(builder.Configuration.GetSection("Logging"));

// 2. Add services, controllers, etc.
builder.Services.AddControllers();

// (Optional) Add custom middleware or anything else
var app = builder.Build();

// 3. Add middleware pipeline
app.UseHttpsRedirection();

// Example: custom request-response logging middleware (see section 4)
app.UseMiddleware<RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware>();

app.UseAuthorization();
app.MapControllers();

app.Run();


appsettings.json (logging configuration)

{
  "Logging": {
    "LogLevel": {
      "Default": "Information",
      "Microsoft": "Warning",
      "Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime": "Information"
    }
  }
}
You can override per environment (e.g. appsettings.Development.json).  




2. Using ILogger<T>


In your controllers, services, etc., inject ILogger<T> and write log statements:

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

[ApiController]
[Route("[controller]")]
public class SampleController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly ILogger<SampleController> _logger;

    public SampleController(ILogger<SampleController> logger)
    {
        _logger = logger;
    }

    [HttpGet("hello")]
    public IActionResult Hello(string name)
    {
        _logger.LogInformation("Hello endpoint called with name = {Name}", name);

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(name))
        {
            _logger.LogWarning("Name was null or empty!");
            return BadRequest("Name required");
        }

        try
        {
            var resp = $"Hello, {name}";
            _logger.LogDebug("Returning response: {Resp}", resp);
            return Ok(resp);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Error in Hello endpoint for name {Name}", name);
            return StatusCode(500, "Internal server error");
        }
    }
}
Key points:


  • Use structured logging (i.e. message templates with {Name}) so fields get captured.

  • Use the appropriate log level: LogTrace, LogDebug, LogInformation, LogWarning, LogError, LogCritical.

  • Always pass the exception into LogError when catching exceptions.




3. Custom Middleware to Log Requests & Responses


If you want more visibility (for example, log the HTTP request body, headers, etc.), you can create a middleware:

public class RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly ILogger<RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware> _logger;

    public RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware(RequestDelegate next, ILogger<RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware> logger)
    {
        _next = next;
        _logger = logger;
    }

    public async Task Invoke(HttpContext context)
    {
        // Log request
        _logger.LogInformation("Incoming request: {Method} {Path}", context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path);

        // (Optional) read & log body — careful: reading the body stream needs enabling buffering
        context.Request.EnableBuffering();
        using (var reader = new StreamReader(context.Request.Body, leaveOpen: true))
        {
            var body = await reader.ReadToEndAsync();
            context.Request.Body.Position = 0;
            _logger.LogDebug("Request Body: {Body}", body);
        }

        // Capture the response by using a response buffer
        var originalBodyStream = context.Response.Body;
        using var responseBody = new MemoryStream();
        context.Response.Body = responseBody;

        try
        {
            await _next(context); // call the rest of the pipeline

            // Read response
            context.Response.Body.Seek(0, SeekOrigin.Begin);
            string respText = await new StreamReader(context.Response.Body).ReadToEndAsync();
            context.Response.Body.Seek(0, SeekOrigin.Begin);

            _logger.LogDebug("Response Status: {StatusCode}, Body: {RespBody}", 
                context.Response.StatusCode, respText);

            // Copy back to the original stream
            await responseBody.CopyToAsync(originalBodyStream);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Exception in processing request: {Method} {Path}",
                context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path);
            throw;
        }
    }
}
Then in Program.cs:

app.UseMiddleware<RequestResponseLoggingMiddleware>();
This gives you granular logs for requests and responses. Be cautious about logging sensitive data (PII).

6. Matching Your Patterns: ilogger_microsoft / nlog / serilog


Based on the patterns you provided:


  • ilogger_microsoft → identifies use of Microsoft’s built-in logging (via AddLogging(...))

  • nlog → identifies NLog-related usage (LogManager.GetCurrentClassLogger, etc.)

  • serilog → identifies Serilog usage (UseSerilog, Log.ForContext, etc.)


In a real codebase, you might see:


  • Microsoft logging style:

builder.Services.AddLogging();
logger.LogInformation(...);


  • NLog style:

var logger = NLog.LogManager.GetCurrentClassLogger();
logger.Info("something");
NLog.LogManager.LoadConfiguration("nlog.config");


  • Serilog style:

Log.ForContext<YourClass>().Information("something");
builder.Host.UseSerilog();
builder.Logging.AddSerilog();


You can combine them by having the Microsoft abstraction layer in your code (ILogger<T>), but back them with providers like NLog or Serilog. That way, your code is provider-agnostic.




7. Best Practices & Considerations


  • Don’t over-log: excessive logging hurts performance and makes logs noisy.

  • Guard expensive log content: if formatting or gathering log message data is expensive, check if (_logger.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Debug)) { … }.

  • Avoid logging sensitive data (passwords, PII).

  • Use structured logging so querying / filtering is easier.

  • Log exceptions with the Exception parameter, not just ex.Message.

  • Use scopes (e.g. _logger.BeginScope(...)) to group related log messages.

  • Rotate logs / limit log size (e.g. Serilog file rolling, NLog archive settings).

  • Centralize configuration (via appsettings.json, nlog.config, etc.).

  • Ensure consistency: don’t mix raw Console.WriteLine or Debug.WriteLine in production logic.

using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

public class SecureEntityService
{
    private readonly AppDbContext _db;
    private readonly ILogger<SecureEntityService> _logger;
    private readonly IAuthorizationService _auth;

    public SecureEntityService(AppDbContext db, ILogger<SecureEntityService> logger, IAuthorizationService auth)
    {
        _db = db;
        _logger = logger;
        _auth = auth;
    }

    [Authorize(Policy = "CanModifyData")]
    public async Task UpdateEntityAsync(int id, string newData, string userId)
    {
        await using var tx = await _db.Database.BeginTransactionAsync();
        try
        {
            var entity = await _db.SecureEntities.FindAsync(id);
            if (entity == null) throw new Exception("Entity not found");

            // Verify integrity before modification
            var recomputed = IntegrityHelper.ComputeHash(entity.SensitiveData);
            if (recomputed != entity.IntegrityHash)
            {
                _logger.LogError("Integrity violation detected for entity {Id}", id);
                throw new Exception("Integrity check failed");
            }

            // Update values
            entity.SensitiveData = newData;
            entity.IntegrityHash = IntegrityHelper.ComputeHash(newData);
            entity.ModifiedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
            entity.ModifiedBy = userId;

            await _db.SaveChangesAsync(); // transactional by default
            await tx.CommitAsync();

            _logger.LogInformation("Entity {Id} updated by {User}", id, userId);
        }
        catch (DbUpdateConcurrencyException ex)
        {
            _logger.LogWarning(ex, "Concurrency conflict while updating entity {Id}", id);
            throw; // or return conflict response
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Update failed for entity {Id}", id);
            await tx.RollbackAsync();
            throw;
        }
    }
}

using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

public class SymmetricCryptoService
{
    private readonly byte[] _key;
    private readonly byte[] _iv;

    public SymmetricCryptoService(byte[] key, byte[] iv)
    {
        _key = key;
        _iv = iv;
    }

    public byte[] Encrypt(string plaintext)
    {
        using var aes = Aes.Create(); // matches your dotnet_security_encrypt_decrypt pattern
        aes.Key = _key;
        aes.IV = _iv;

        using var ms = new MemoryStream();
        using var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, aes.CreateEncryptor(), CryptoStreamMode.Write);
        using var writer = new StreamWriter(cs, Encoding.UTF8);

        writer.Write(plaintext);
        writer.Flush();
        cs.FlushFinalBlock();

        return ms.ToArray();
    }

    public string Decrypt(byte[] cipher)
    {
        using var aes = Aes.Create();
        aes.Key = _key;
        aes.IV = _iv;

        using var ms = new MemoryStream(cipher);
        using var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, aes.CreateDecryptor(), CryptoStreamMode.Read);
        using var reader = new StreamReader(cs, Encoding.UTF8);

        return reader.ReadToEnd();
    }
}

public class AesGcmService
{

    public AesGcmService(byte[] key) => _key = key;

    public (byte[] Nonce, byte[] Ciphertext, byte[] Tag) Encrypt(string plaintext)
    {

        var nonce = RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(12); // 96-bit nonce
        var ciphertext = new byte[plaintextBytes.Length];
        var tag = new byte[16];

        aes.Encrypt(nonce, plaintextBytes, ciphertext, tag);

        return (nonce, ciphertext, tag);

    {
        var plaintextBytes = new byte[ciphertext.Length];
        using var aes = new AesGcm(_key);
        aes.Decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, tag, plaintextBytes);

        return System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetString(plaintextBytes);
    }

var dobEnc = aes.Encrypt(dob);

// Save ciphertext pieces to the patient record

patient.SSNNonce = ssnEnc.Nonce;
patient.SSNTag = ssnEnc.Tag;

patient.DoBCipher = dobEnc.Ciphertext;
patient.DoBNonce = dobEnc.Nonce;
patient.DoBTag = dobEnc.Tag;

Console.WriteLine("Patient PHI encrypted and ready to save to DB.");

1. Enforce HTTPS everywhere (Kestrel + HSTS + redirect)


Program.cs

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Kestrel HTTPS options (if self-hosting w/ certificate)
builder.WebHost.ConfigureKestrel(options =>
{
    options.ConfigureHttpsDefaults(httpsOptions =>
    {
        httpsOptions.SslProtocols = System.Security.Authentication.SslProtocols.Tls12
                                    | System.Security.Authentication.SslProtocols.Tls13;
    });
    // Example: listen with TLS (production: use proper cert store / Key Vault)
    // options.ListenAnyIP(5001, lo => lo.UseHttps("cert.pfx", "pfxPassword"));
});

builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddHsts(opts =>
{
    opts.Preload = true;
    opts.IncludeSubDomains = true;
    opts.MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365);
});

var app = builder.Build();

app.UseForwardedHeaders();    // if behind proxy (configure KnownProxies in prod)
app.UseHsts();                // production only
app.UseHttpsRedirection();    // redirect HTTP → HTTPS
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
Notes


  • Enforce TLS 1.2+ (prefer TLS 1.3 when available).

  • Use ForwardedHeaders when behind reverse proxies so scheme detection (http/https) is accurate.

  • Do not serve PHI over HTTP. Block HTTP endpoints in production.




2. Use IHttpClientFactory and configure handlers (do not accept invalid certs)


Registration

builder.Services.AddHttpClient("SecureApi", client =>
{
    client.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.trusted.example");
    client.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
})
.ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() =>
{
    var handler = new HttpClientHandler
    {
        // Use platform defaults; set allowed TLS versions
        SslProtocols = System.Security.Authentication.SslProtocols.Tls12
                       | System.Security.Authentication.SslProtocols.Tls13
    };

    // Optional certificate pinning logic: validate expected thumbprint
    handler.ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback = (request, cert, chain, errors) =>
    {
        if (errors != System.Net.Security.SslPolicyErrors.None) return false;
        // Example pin (replace with actual thumbprint check if desired)
        // return cert.GetCertHashString() == "EXPECTED_THUMBPRINT";
        return true;
    };

    return handler;
});
Usage

public class ExternalApiService
{
    private readonly IHttpClientFactory _factory;

    public ExternalApiService(IHttpClientFactory factory) => _factory = factory;

    public async Task<string> GetPatientDataAsync(string patientId)
    {
        var client = _factory.CreateClient("SecureApi");
        var resp = await client.GetAsync($"/patients/{patientId}");
        resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        return await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync();
    }
}
Do NOT use ServicePointManager.ServerCertificateValidationCallback = (s,c,chain,errors) => true; — that bypasses certificate validation and is a critical vulnerability.




3. WebSockets / SignalR — run over WSS and require authorization


Startup

builder.Services.AddSignalR();

app.UseRouting();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.UseEndpoints(endpoints =>
{
    endpoints.MapHub<MyHub>("/hubs/notifications").RequireAuthorization();
});
Hub

[Authorize]
public class MyHub : Hub
{
    public async Task SendPatientUpdate(string patientId, string payload)
    {
        // Authorization and message-level integrity should be enforced server-side
        await Clients.Group(patientId).SendAsync("Receive", payload);
    }
}
Note: SignalR will use WSS automatically when the page is served over HTTPS. Require [Authorize] to prevent unauthorized subscriptions.




4. Raw sockets: if you must, use SslStream (example)


Server

var listener = new TcpListener(IPAddress.Any, 9000);
listener.Start();
while (true)
{
    var client = await listener.AcceptTcpClientAsync();
    _ = Task.Run(async () =>
    {
        using var stream = client.GetStream();
        using var ssl = new SslStream(stream, leaveInnerStreamOpen: false);
        // serverCertificate loaded from secure store (do not embed in code)
        await ssl.AuthenticateAsServerAsync(serverCertificate, clientCertificateRequired: false,
            enabledSslProtocols: SslProtocols.Tls12 | SslProtocols.Tls13, checkCertificateRevocation: true);

        // read/write via ssl
    });
}
Client

using var tcp = new TcpClient("server.example", 9000);
using var ssl = new SslStream(tcp.GetStream(), false, (sender, cert, chain, errors) =>
{
    return errors == SslPolicyErrors.None;
});
await ssl.AuthenticateAsClientAsync("server.example", null, SslProtocols.Tls12 | SslProtocols.Tls13, true);
Tip: never leave certificate validation permissive on client side.




5. Application-level message integrity (HMAC) — for multi-hop / queued data


TLS protects transport hop-by-hop. If messages traverse intermediaries (message queues, logs, databases) or must be validated end-to-end, use HMAC or signatures.


HMAC helper

public static class IntegrityUtils
{
    public static byte[] ComputeHmac(byte[] key, byte[] data)
    {
        using var h = new HMACSHA256(key);
        return h.ComputeHash(data);
    }

    public static bool VerifyHmac(byte[] key, byte[] data, byte[] expectedMac)
    {
        var computed = ComputeHmac(key, data);
        return CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(computed, expectedMac);
    }
}
Sender
  • Serialize payload (UTF8 JSON) → compute HMAC with server-side secret key → send payload + mac (or store together).


Receiver
  • Recompute HMAC from received payload → use FixedTimeEquals to compare → reject and alert on mismatch.


Key management: HMAC key is a secret — store in Key Vault/HSM and rotate per policy.




6. Don’t put PHI in URLs or logs; mask logs


  • Avoid query strings for ePHI: GET /patient?ssn=... is bad (proxies, browser history, server logs). Use request bodies or POST.

  • Mask PHI in logs. Example with ILogger<T>:

public void ProcessPatient(string patientId, string ssn)
{
    string maskedSsn = ssn.Length >= 4 ? ssn[^4..].PadLeft(ssn.Length, '*') : "****";
    _logger.LogInformation("Processing patient {PatientId}, SSN={SSN}", patientId, maskedSsn);
}

  • Consider a logging filter or middleware that redacts configured keys (ssn, dob, mrn) from JSON request bodies before logging.


7. Short example: end-to-end flow (client posts PHI with HMAC)


Sender (client)

var payloadJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(patientPayload);
var payloadBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(payloadJson);
var mac = IntegrityUtils.ComputeHmac(hmacKey, payloadBytes);

var content = new MultipartFormDataContent
{
    { new StringContent(payloadJson, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"), "payload" },
    { new StringContent(Convert.ToBase64String(mac)), "mac" }
};

var client = _factory.CreateClient("SecureApi");
var resp = await client.PostAsync("/api/patients", content);
Receiver (server)

[HttpPost("api/patients")]
public async Task<IActionResult> PostPatient()
{
    var payloadJson = await Request.Form["payload"].FirstOrDefaultAsync();
    var macBase64 = await Request.Form["mac"].FirstOrDefaultAsync();

    var payloadBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(payloadJson);
    var mac = Convert.FromBase64String(macBase64);

    if (!IntegrityUtils.VerifyHmac(hmacKeyFromKeyVault, payloadBytes, mac))
    {
        _logger.LogWarning("HMAC verification failed for incoming PHI");
        return StatusCode(403, "Integrity check failed");
    }

    // process
    return Ok();
}
Note: HMAC key (hmacKeyFromKeyVault) must come from secure store (Key Vault) and never be logged.




Final note
TLS is the baseline. Add application-level integrity controls (HMAC/AES-GCM) when the architecture has terminations (load balancers, proxies, message queues) or multi-hop delivery where end-to-end detection of tampering is required. Use IHttpClientFactory, AesGcm/HMACSHA256, Key Vault for keys, and add CI scanners to catch bypasses.

Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/?view=aspnetcore-9.0

In .NET, this typically means:


  • Assigning a unique ID (e.g., Guid, UserId) to every user.

  • Ensuring database-level constraints to prevent duplicates.

  • Using authentication mechanisms tied to that ID (e.g., JWT, cookies, claims).


 1. Code-First Approach (Entity Framework Core)

In Code-First, you define models and let EF generate the database schema.


Example: User Entity with Unique Identifier

using System;
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

public class ApplicationUser
{
    [Key]
    public Guid UserId { get; set; } = Guid.NewGuid(); // Unique ID

    [Required]
    [MaxLength(100)]
    public string Username { get; set; }

    [Required]
    [EmailAddress]
    public string Email { get; set; }

    public string PasswordHash { get; set; }
}

public class AppDbContext : DbContext
{
    public DbSet<ApplicationUser> Users { get; set; }

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        // Unique index on Email (no duplicate users)
        modelBuilder.Entity<ApplicationUser>()
            .HasIndex(u => u.Email)
            .IsUnique();

        base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
    }

    protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options)
        => options.UseSqlServer("Server=.;Database=HIPAA_DB;Trusted_Connection=True;");
}


Explanation


  • UserId uses Guid.NewGuid() to ensure uniqueness.

  • .HasIndex(u => u.Email).IsUnique() enforces unique email addresses at the DB level.

  • [Key] and [Required] ensure integrity and enforce primary key rules.


 Usage Example

using (var db = new AppDbContext())
{
    var user = new ApplicationUser
    {
        Username = "mostafiz",
        Email = "mostafiz@example.com",
        PasswordHash = "hashed_password_here"
    };

    db.Users.Add(user);
    db.SaveChanges();

    Console.WriteLine($"User created with ID: {user.UserId}");
}


2. Database-First Approach (EF Model from Existing DB)

In Database-First, the database schema already exists, and EF maps it to C# models.


SQL Schema Example

CREATE TABLE Users (
    UserId UNIQUEIDENTIFIER NOT NULL DEFAULT NEWID(),
    Username NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Email NVARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    PasswordHash NVARCHAR(255),
    PRIMARY KEY (UserId)
);


EF Model (Auto-Generated)

public partial class User
{
    public Guid UserId { get; set; }
    public string Username { get; set; } = null!;
    public string Email { get; set; } = null!;
    public string PasswordHash { get; set; }
}


 Verification Example

using (var db = new HIPAA_DBContext())
{
    var userExists = db.Users.Any(u => u.Email == "mostafiz@example.com");

    if (!userExists)
    {
        db.Users.Add(new User
        {
            UserId = Guid.NewGuid(),
            Username = "mostafiz",
            Email = "mostafiz@example.com",
            PasswordHash = "hashed_password_here"
        });
        db.SaveChanges();
    }
}

 Best Practices


  • Always use GUIDs for user identification, not sequential integers (harder to guess).

  • Enforce uniqueness at both code and DB levels.

  • In authentication (e.g., JWT, ASP.NET Identity), ensure the sub or NameIdentifier claim holds the unique UserId.

  • For external integrations (APIs, SSO), use UUID-based claims instead of usernames.

To implement secure, verifiable user authentication in .NET applications using:


  • ASP.NET Core Identity or OAuth (OpenID Connect)

  • Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

5. Enforce Anti-Forgery Protection


Protect authentication endpoints (especially those handling PHI) against CSRF attacks.

[HttpPost]

MD5 is a fast 128-bit hash but insecure due to collision vulnerabilities, making it unsuitable for cryptography. In contrast, SHA-256 is slower but far more secure, offering strong resistance against modern attacks (NIST, 2015).

You can use the following safe code

MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");


Reference:
National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2015). Secure Hash Standard (SHS), FIPS PUB 180-4. https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4

All electronic Protected Health Information (PHI) stored or cached by the Express application must be encrypted at rest using strong, industry-standard algorithms (AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305). Sensitive fields (e.g., patient name, SSN, medical record number) must never be stored in plaintext.

1. Encrypt PHI at Rest (AES-256-GCM) 
const crypto = require('crypto');

// Encryption configuration
const ALGORITHM = 'aes-256-gcm';
const KEY = Buffer.from(process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY, 'hex'); // Must be 32 bytes (64 hex chars)

/**
 * Encrypts PHI data using AES-256-GCM
 * @param {string} plaintext - Sensitive PHI data
 * @returns {string} - Encrypted data with IV and auth tag (format: iv:authTag:ciphertext)
 */
function encryptPHI(plaintext) {
  if (!plaintext) return null;
  
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(16); // Generate random IV
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv(ALGORITHM, KEY, iv);
  
  let ciphertext = cipher.update(plaintext, 'utf8', 'hex');
  ciphertext += cipher.final('hex');
  
  const authTag = cipher.getAuthTag().toString('hex');
  
  // Return IV:authTag:ciphertext (all needed for decryption)
  return `${iv.toString('hex')}:${authTag}:${ciphertext}`;
}

/**
 * Decrypts PHI data
 * @param {string} encrypted - Encrypted data (iv:authTag:ciphertext)
 * @returns {string} - Decrypted plaintext
 */
function decryptPHI(encrypted) {
  if (!encrypted) return null;
  
  const [ivHex, authTagHex, ciphertext] = encrypted.split(':');
  const iv = Buffer.from(ivHex, 'hex');
  const authTag = Buffer.from(authTagHex, 'hex');
  
  const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv(ALGORITHM, KEY, iv);
  decipher.setAuthTag(authTag);
  
  let plaintext = decipher.update(ciphertext, 'hex', 'utf8');
  plaintext += decipher.final('utf8');
  
  return plaintext;
}

// Example usage:
const patientSSN = '123-45-6789';
const encryptedSSN = encryptPHI(patientSSN);
// Store encryptedSSN in database

// Later, when retrieving:
const decryptedSSN = decryptPHI(encryptedSSN);

2. Database-Level Encryption (MongoDB Example with mongoose-encryption)
const mongoose = require('mongoose');
const encrypt = require('mongoose-field-encryption').fieldEncryption;

const patientSchema = new mongoose.Schema({
  name: { type: String, required: true },
  ssn: { type: String, required: true },
  medicalRecordNumber: { type: String, required: true },
  email: String
});

// Encrypt specific fields
patientSchema.plugin(encrypt, {
  fields: ['ssn', 'medicalRecordNumber'], // ← Encrypt PHI fields only
  secret: process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY,
  saltGenerator: () => crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex')
});

const Patient = mongoose.model('Patient', patientSchema);

// Usage: encryption/decryption happens automatically
const patient = new Patient({
  name: 'John Doe',
  ssn: '123-45-6789', // ← Will be encrypted before saving
  medicalRecordNumber: 'MRN123456'
});
await patient.save(); // PHI fields encrypted in DB

All HIPAA-covered applications must implement comprehensive audit logging to track who accessed PHI, when, and what actions were performed. Audit logs must be tamper-resistant, retained for at least 6 years, and never contain actual PHI data.

const winston = require('winston');
const crypto = require('crypto');

// ==================== WINSTON LOGGER SETUP ====================

const auditLogger = winston.createLogger({
  level: 'info',
  format: winston.format.combine(
    winston.format.timestamp(),
    winston.format.json()
  ),
  transports: [
    new winston.transports.File({ 
      filename: 'logs/audit.log',
      maxsize: 50000000, // 50MB
      maxFiles: null // Keep all files for 6 years HIPAA compliance
    }),
    new winston.transports.File({ 
      filename: 'logs/security.log', 
      level: 'warn' 
    })
  ]
});

// Hash identifiers to anonymize in logs (never log actual PHI)
function hashIdentifier(id) {
  if (!id) return 'unknown';
  return crypto.createHash('sha256')
    .update(id + process.env.AUDIT_SALT)
    .digest('hex')
    .substring(0, 16);
}

// ==================== AUDIT MIDDLEWARE ====================

const auditMiddleware = (req, res, next) => {
  const startTime = Date.now();
  const originalSend = res.send;
  
  res.send = function(data) {
    const isPHI = ['/api/patients', '/api/records', '/api/appointments'].some(r => req.path.startsWith(r));
    
    auditLogger.info({
      eventType: isPHI ? 'PHI_ACCESS' : 'API_REQUEST',
      userId: req.session?.userId ? hashIdentifier(req.session.userId) : 'anonymous',
      method: req.method,
      path: req.path,
      statusCode: res.statusCode,
      duration: `${Date.now() - startTime}ms`,
      ip: req.ip,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      isPHI: isPHI
    });
    
    return originalSend.call(this, data);
  };
  
  next();
};

// ==================== AUTHENTICATION LOGGING ====================

function logAuthEvent(userId, action, success, ip, reason = null) {
  const level = success ? 'info' : 'warn';
  auditLogger[level]({
    eventType: success ? 'AUTH_SUCCESS' : 'AUTH_FAILURE',
    action: action, // 'LOGIN', 'LOGOUT', 'PASSWORD_RESET'
    userId: hashIdentifier(userId),
    success: success,
    reason: reason,
    ip: ip,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    severity: success ? 'LOW' : 'HIGH'
  });
}

function logAuthorizationFailure(userId, resource, action, ip) {
  auditLogger.warn({
    eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
    action: 'ACCESS_DENIED',
    userId: hashIdentifier(userId),
    resource: resource,
    attemptedAction: action,
    ip: ip,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    severity: 'MEDIUM'
  });
}

// ==================== PHI ACCESS LOGGING ====================

function logPHIAccess(userId, patientId, action, resourceType, ip) {
  const level = ['DELETE', 'EXPORT'].includes(action) ? 'warn' : 'info';
  auditLogger[level]({
    eventType: action === 'EXPORT' ? 'PHI_EXPORT' : 'PHI_ACCESS',
    action: action, // 'VIEW', 'CREATE', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE', 'EXPORT'
    userId: hashIdentifier(userId),
    patientId: hashIdentifier(patientId),
    resourceType: resourceType, // 'MEDICAL_RECORD', 'LAB_RESULT', 'PRESCRIPTION'
    ip: ip,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    isPHI: true,
    severity: ['DELETE', 'EXPORT'].includes(action) ? 'HIGH' : 'MEDIUM'
  });
}

  legacyMode: true
});

redisClient.connect().catch(console.error);

    sameSite: 'strict',
    maxAge: 15 * 60 * 1000 // 15 minutes absolute timeout
  }
};

const INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes in milliseconds

const inactivityMiddleware = (req, res, next) => {
  // Skip timeout check for public routes
  const publicRoutes = ['/api/auth/login', '/api/auth/register', '/health'];
  if (publicRoutes.includes(req.path)) {
    return next();
  }

  // Check if user is authenticated
  if (!req.session || !req.session.userId) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Not authenticated' });
  }

  const now = Date.now();
  const lastActivity = req.session.lastActivity || now;
  const timeSinceLastActivity = now - lastActivity;

  // Check if session expired due to inactivity
  if (timeSinceLastActivity > INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT) {
    req.session.destroy((err) => {
      if (err) console.error('Session destroy error:', err);
    });
    
    return res.status(401).json({ 
      error: 'Session expired due to inactivity',
      reason: 'INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT'
    });
  }

  // Update last activity timestamp
  req.session.lastActivity = now;
  req.session.touch(); // Extend session expiration
  
  next();
};

    {

      issuer: 'MyApp',
      audience: 'MyApp-API'
    }
  );

// Verify JWT token middleware
function verifyToken(req, res, next) {
  const authHeader = req.headers['authorization'];
  const token = authHeader && authHeader.split(' ')[1]; // Bearer TOKEN
  
  if (!token) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Access token required' });
  }

    }

A HIPAA-enabled app must implement strict authorization controls before allowing deletion or modification of PHI. Use role-based access control (RBAC), audit all destructive operations, and consider implementing soft deletes to maintain data integrity and compliance.

const express = require('express');

// ==================== ROLE-BASED ACCESS CONTROL (RBAC) ====================

const ROLES = {
  ADMIN: 'admin',
  DOCTOR: 'doctor',
  NURSE: 'nurse',
  PATIENT: 'patient',
  READONLY: 'readonly'
};

const PERMISSIONS = {
  READ_PHI: 'read_phi',
  CREATE_PHI: 'create_phi',
  UPDATE_PHI: 'update_phi',
  DELETE_PHI: 'delete_phi',
  EXPORT_PHI: 'export_phi'
};

// Define role permissions
const rolePermissions = {
  [ROLES.ADMIN]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.CREATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.UPDATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.DELETE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.EXPORT_PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.DOCTOR]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.CREATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.UPDATE_PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.NURSE]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.CREATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.UPDATE_PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.PATIENT]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.READONLY]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI
  ]
};

// ==================== AUTHORIZATION MIDDLEWARE ====================

function requirePermission(permission) {
  return async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      // Get user from database
      const user = await db.users.findById(req.userId);
      
      if (!user) {
        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'User not found' });
      }
      
      // Check if user's role has the required permission
      const userPermissions = rolePermissions[user.role] || [];
      
      if (!userPermissions.includes(permission)) {
        // Log authorization failure
        auditLogger.warn({
          eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
          userId: req.userId,
          permission: permission,
          role: user.role,
          resource: req.path,
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
        });
        
        return res.status(403).json({ 
          error: 'Insufficient permissions',
          required: permission,
          userRole: user.role
        });
      }
      
      // Store user info for later use
      req.user = user;
      next();
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Authorization error:', error);
      res.status(500).json({ error: 'Authorization check failed' });
    }
  };
}

// Check if user owns the resource
async function requireOwnership(req, res, next) {
  const { patientId } = req.params;
  
  // Allow admins to access any resource
  if (req.user.role === ROLES.ADMIN) {
    return next();
  }
  
  // Check if patient is accessing their own data
  if (req.user.id === patientId) {
    return next();
  }
  
  // Check if doctor/nurse has access to this patient
  const hasAccess = await db.patientAccess.exists({
    userId: req.user.id,
    patientId: patientId
  });
  
  if (!hasAccess) {
    auditLogger.warn({
      eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
      reason: 'OWNERSHIP_CHECK_FAILED',
      userId: req.user.id,
      patientId: patientId,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
    });
    
    return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Access denied to this resource' });
  }
  
  next();
}

// ==================== SOFT DELETE IMPLEMENTATION ====================

// Soft delete (recommended for HIPAA compliance)
async function softDeleteRecord(req, res) {
  const { recordId } = req.params;
  
  try {
    // Update record with deleted flag instead of actually deleting
    const record = await db.records.update(
      { id: recordId },
      { 
        isDeleted: true,
        deletedAt: new Date(),
        deletedBy: req.user.id,
        deletionReason: req.body.reason || 'Not specified'
      }
    );
    
    // Log deletion event
    auditLogger.warn({
      eventType: 'PHI_SOFT_DELETE',
      userId: req.user.id,
      recordId: recordId,
      reason: req.body.reason,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      severity: 'HIGH'
    });
    
    res.json({ message: 'Record deleted successfully', recordId: recordId });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Soft delete error:', error);
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Delete operation failed' });
  }
}

// Hard delete (only for admins with MFA)
async function hardDeleteRecord(req, res) {
  const { recordId } = req.params;
  
  try {
    // Verify MFA token before hard delete
    const { mfaToken } = req.body;
    
    if (!mfaToken || !verifyMFAToken(req.user.mfaSecret, mfaToken)) {
      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'MFA verification required for permanent deletion' });
    }
    
    // Permanently delete the record
    await db.records.delete({ id: recordId });
    
    // Log hard deletion event
    auditLogger.error({
      eventType: 'PHI_HARD_DELETE',
      action: 'PERMANENT_DELETION',
      userId: req.user.id,
      recordId: recordId,
      reason: req.body.reason,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      severity: 'CRITICAL'
    });
    
    res.json({ message: 'Record permanently deleted', recordId: recordId });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Hard delete error:', error);
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Permanent delete operation failed' });
  }
}

// ==================== UPDATE WITH AUTHORIZATION ====================

async function updateRecord(req, res) {
  const { recordId } = req.params;
  const updates = req.body;
  
  try {
    // Get original record for audit trail
    const originalRecord = await db.records.findById(recordId);
    
    if (!originalRecord) {
      return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Record not found' });
    }
    
    // Update the record
    const updatedRecord = await db.records.update(
      { id: recordId },
      { 
        ...updates,
        updatedAt: new Date(),
        updatedBy: req.user.id
      }
    );
    
    // Log modification event
    auditLogger.info({
      eventType: 'PHI_UPDATE',
      userId: req.user.id,
      recordId: recordId,
      changedFields: Object.keys(updates),
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      isPHI: true
    });
    
    res.json({ message: 'Record updated successfully', record: updatedRecord });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Update error:', error);
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Update operation failed' });
  }
}

class AuthorizationError extends Error {

    this.resource = resource;

All electronic Protected Health Information (PHI) must be encrypted at rest using strong, industry-standard algorithms (AES-256-GCM recommended). Sensitive data fields must never be stored in plaintext. Use proper key management and secure hashing for passwords.

const crypto = require('crypto');
const bcrypt = require('bcrypt');

// ==================== AES-256-GCM ENCRYPTION (RECOMMENDED) ====================

const ALGORITHM = 'aes-256-gcm';
const KEY = Buffer.from(process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY, 'hex'); // Must be 32 bytes (64 hex chars)
const IV_LENGTH = 16; // 16 bytes for AES
const AUTH_TAG_LENGTH = 16; // 16 bytes for GCM authentication tag

// Encrypt PHI data
function encryptPHI(plaintext) {
  if (!plaintext) return null;
  
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(IV_LENGTH);
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv(ALGORITHM, KEY, iv);
  
  let ciphertext = cipher.update(plaintext, 'utf8', 'hex');
  ciphertext += cipher.final('hex');
  
  const authTag = cipher.getAuthTag().toString('hex');
  
  // Return format: iv:authTag:ciphertext
  return `${iv.toString('hex')}:${authTag}:${ciphertext}`;
}

// Decrypt PHI data
function decryptPHI(encrypted) {
  if (!encrypted) return null;
  
  const [ivHex, authTagHex, ciphertext] = encrypted.split(':');
  
  const iv = Buffer.from(ivHex, 'hex');
  const authTag = Buffer.from(authTagHex, 'hex');
  
  const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv(ALGORITHM, KEY, iv);
  decipher.setAuthTag(authTag);
  
  let plaintext = decipher.update(ciphertext, 'hex', 'utf8');
  plaintext += decipher.final('utf8');
  
  return plaintext;
}

// ==================== PASSWORD HASHING (BCRYPT) ====================

const SALT_ROUNDS = 12;

// Hash password
async function hashPassword(plainPassword) {
  return await bcrypt.hash(plainPassword, SALT_ROUNDS);
}

// Verify password
async function verifyPassword(plainPassword, hashedPassword) {
  return await bcrypt.compare(plainPassword, hashedPassword);
}

// ==================== SHA-256 HASHING (FOR AUDIT LOGS) ====================

// One-way hash for audit trails (NOT for PHI that needs retrieval)
function hashForAudit(data) {
  if (!data) return null;
  
  return crypto
    .createHash('sha256')
    .update(data + process.env.HASH_SALT)
    .digest('hex');
}

// ==================== KEY GENERATION ====================

// Generate encryption key (run once, store securely)
function generateEncryptionKey() {
  // Generate 256-bit (32 bytes) key
  const key = crypto.randomBytes(32);
  console.log('Encryption Key (hex):', key.toString('hex'));
  console.log('Store this in environment variable: ENCRYPTION_KEY');
  return key.toString('hex');
}

// Generate salt for hashing
function generateSalt() {
  const salt = crypto.randomBytes(32);
  console.log('Hash Salt (hex):', salt.toString('hex'));
  console.log('Store this in environment variable: HASH_SALT');
  return salt.toString('hex');
}

  return {
    id: patientData.id,
    // Encrypt sensitive fields
    name: encryptPHI(patientData.name),
    ssn: encryptPHI(patientData.ssn),

    ssn: decryptPHI(encryptedData.ssn),

});

});

  });

}

const express = require('express');
const https = require('https');
const helmet = require('helmet');
const axios = require('axios');

const app = express();

// ==================== FORCE HTTPS/TLS ====================

// Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
function forceHTTPS(req, res, next) {
  if (!req.secure && req.get('x-forwarded-proto') !== 'https') {
    return res.redirect(301, `https://${req.get('host')}${req.url}`);
  }
  next();
}

app.use(forceHTTPS);

// ==================== SECURE HEADERS (HELMET) ====================

app.use(helmet({
  // HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
  hsts: {
    maxAge: 31536000, // 1 year in seconds
    includeSubDomains: true,
    preload: true
  },
  
  // Content Security Policy
  contentSecurityPolicy: {
    directives: {
      defaultSrc: ["'self'"],
      scriptSrc: ["'self'"],
      connectSrc: ["'self'"],
      upgradeInsecureRequests: [] // Force HTTPS for all resources
    }
  },
  
  // Prevent MIME type sniffing
  noSniff: true,
  
  // XSS Protection
  xssFilter: true,
  
  // Disable X-Powered-By
  hidePoweredBy: true
}));

// ==================== TLS/SSL CONFIGURATION FOR OUTGOING REQUESTS ====================

// Secure HTTPS agent for API calls
const secureHttpsAgent = new https.Agent({
  rejectUnauthorized: true, // Reject invalid/self-signed certificates
  minVersion: 'TLSv1.2', // Minimum TLS 1.2
  maxVersion: 'TLSv1.3', // Prefer TLS 1.3
  
  // Strong cipher suites
  ciphers: [
    'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256',
    'ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384',
    'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256',
    'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384'
  ].join(':'),
  
  honorCipherOrder: true
});

// Make secure API call with TLS validation
async function makeSecureAPICall(url, data, authToken) {
  try {
    const response = await axios({
      method: 'POST',
      url: url,
      data: data,
      httpsAgent: secureHttpsAgent,
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${authToken}`,
        'User-Agent': 'MyApp/1.0',
        'X-Request-ID': generateRequestId()
      },
      timeout: 30000 // 30 seconds timeout
    });
    
    return response.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Secure API call failed:', error.message);
    throw new Error('Failed to communicate securely with external service');
  }
}

// ==================== REQUEST/RESPONSE ENCRYPTION ====================

const crypto = require('crypto');

// Encrypt sensitive data before transmission
function encryptForTransmission(data, publicKey) {
  const buffer = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(data));
  
  const encrypted = crypto.publicEncrypt(
    {
      key: publicKey,
      padding: crypto.constants.RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING,
      oaepHash: 'sha256'
    },
    buffer
  );
  
  return encrypted.toString('base64');
}

// Decrypt received encrypted data
function decryptFromTransmission(encryptedData, privateKey) {
  const buffer = Buffer.from(encryptedData, 'base64');
  
  const decrypted = crypto.privateDecrypt(
    {
      key: privateKey,
      padding: crypto.constants.RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING,
      oaepHash: 'sha256'
    },
    buffer
  );
  
  return JSON.parse(decrypted.toString('utf8'));
}

// ==================== WEBHOOK SECURITY ====================

// Verify webhook signature (e.g., from Stripe, GitHub, etc.)
function verifyWebhookSignature(req, res, next) {
  const signature = req.headers['x-webhook-signature'];
  const secret = process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET;
  
  if (!signature) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Missing webhook signature' });
  }
  
  const expectedSignature = crypto
    .createHmac('sha256', secret)
    .update(req.rawBody) // Requires raw body parser
    .digest('hex');
  
  if (!crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signature), Buffer.from(expectedSignature))) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid webhook signature' });
  }
  
  next();
}
