const express = require('express');

// ==================== ROLES AND PERMISSIONS ====================

const ROLES = {
  ADMIN: 'admin',
  DOCTOR: 'doctor',
  NURSE: 'nurse',
  PATIENT: 'patient',
  BILLING: 'billing',
  READONLY: 'readonly'
};

const PERMISSIONS = {
  READ_PHI: 'read_phi',
  CREATE_PHI: 'create_phi',
  UPDATE_PHI: 'update_phi',
  DELETE_PHI: 'delete_phi',
  EXPORT_PHI: 'export_phi',
  MANAGE_USERS: 'manage_users',
  VIEW_AUDIT_LOGS: 'view_audit_logs'
};

// Define permissions for each role
const rolePermissions = {
  [ROLES.ADMIN]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.CREATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.UPDATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.DELETE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.EXPORT_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.MANAGE_USERS,
    PERMISSIONS.VIEW_AUDIT_LOGS
  ],
  [ROLES.DOCTOR]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.CREATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.UPDATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.EXPORT_PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.NURSE]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.CREATE_PHI,
    PERMISSIONS.UPDATE_PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.PATIENT]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI // Can only read their own data
  ],
  [ROLES.BILLING]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI // Limited to billing-related PHI
  ],
  [ROLES.READONLY]: [
    PERMISSIONS.READ_PHI
  ]
};

// ==================== AUTHORIZATION MIDDLEWARE ====================

// Check if user has required permission
function requirePermission(permission) {
  return async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      // Get user from session/token
      const user = await db.users.findById(req.userId);
      
      if (!user) {
        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'User not authenticated' });
      }
      
      // Check if user's role has the required permission
      const userPermissions = rolePermissions[user.role] || [];
      
      if (!userPermissions.includes(permission)) {
        // Log authorization failure for audit
        auditLogger.warn({
          eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
          userId: req.userId,
          userRole: user.role,
          requiredPermission: permission,
          resource: req.path,
          ip: req.ip,
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
        });
        
        return res.status(403).json({ 
          error: 'Insufficient permissions',
          required: permission
        });
      }
      
      // Attach user to request for later use
      req.user = user;
      next();
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Authorization error:', error);
      res.status(500).json({ error: 'Authorization check failed' });
    }
  };
}

// Check if user has any of the specified roles
function requireRole(...allowedRoles) {
  return async (req, res, next) => {
    const user = await db.users.findById(req.userId);
    
    if (!user || !allowedRoles.includes(user.role)) {
      auditLogger.warn({
        eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
        reason: 'ROLE_MISMATCH',
        userId: req.userId,
        userRole: user?.role,
        allowedRoles: allowedRoles,
        resource: req.path,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
      });
      
      return res.status(403).json({ 
        error: 'Access denied',
        allowedRoles: allowedRoles
      });
    }
    
    req.user = user;
    next();
  };
}

// ==================== RESOURCE OWNERSHIP AUTHORIZATION ====================

// Check if user owns the resource or has appropriate access
async function requireOwnershipOrRole(allowedRoles = []) {
  return async (req, res, next) => {
    const { patientId } = req.params;
    
    // Allow specified roles to access any resource
    if (allowedRoles.includes(req.user.role)) {
      return next();
    }
    
    // Check if patient is accessing their own data
    if (req.user.id === patientId) {
      return next();
    }
    
    // Check if healthcare provider has been granted access to this patient
    const hasAccess = await db.patientAccess.exists({
      providerId: req.user.id,
      patientId: patientId,
      accessExpiry: { $gt: new Date() }
    });
    
    if (!hasAccess) {
      auditLogger.warn({
        eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
        reason: 'OWNERSHIP_CHECK_FAILED',
        userId: req.user.id,
        patientId: patientId,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
      });
      
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Access denied to this resource' });
    }
    
    next();
  };
}

// ==================== ATTRIBUTE-BASED ACCESS CONTROL (ABAC) ====================

// Advanced authorization based on multiple attributes
function requireConditions(conditionFn) {
  return async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      const context = {
        user: req.user,
        resource: req.params,
        action: req.method,
        time: new Date(),
        ip: req.ip
      };
      
      const isAuthorized = await conditionFn(context);
      
      if (!isAuthorized) {
        auditLogger.warn({
          eventType: 'AUTHZ_FAILURE',
          reason: 'CONDITION_NOT_MET',
          userId: req.user.id,
          resource: req.path,
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
        });
        
        return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Authorization conditions not met' });
      }
      
      next();
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('ABAC error:', error);
      res.status(500).json({ error: 'Authorization check failed' });
    }
  };
}

// Example ABAC condition: Only allow access during business hours
function businessHoursOnly(context) {
  const hour = context.time.getHours();
  const day = context.time.getDay();
  
  // Monday-Friday, 8 AM - 6 PM
  const isBusinessHours = day >= 1 && day <= 5 && hour >= 8 && hour < 18;
  
  // Admins can access anytime
  if (context.user.role === ROLES.ADMIN) {
    return true;
  }
  
  return isBusinessHours;
}

// ==================== AUTHORIZATION EXCEPTION ====================

class AuthorizationException extends Error {
  constructor(message, userId, resource, requiredPermission) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'AuthorizationException';
    this.userId = userId;
    this.resource = resource;
    this.requiredPermission = requiredPermission;
  }
}

// Throw authorization exception
function denyAccess(userId, resource, requiredPermission) {
  throw new AuthorizationException(
    'Access denied',
    userId,
    resource,
    requiredPermission
  );
}

        // Remove potentially dangerous characters
        req.body[key] = req.body[key]

// Generate checksum for data integrity verification
function generateChecksum(data) {
  return crypto
    .createHash('sha256')
    .update(JSON.stringify(data))
    .digest('hex');
}

// Verify data hasn't been tampered with
function verifyChecksum(data, expectedChecksum) {
  const actualChecksum = generateChecksum(data);
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(actualChecksum),
    Buffer.from(expectedChecksum)
  );
}

// Middleware to add checksum to records
async function addChecksumToRecord(req, res, next) {
  const originalJson = res.json.bind(res);
  
  res.json = function(data) {
    if (data && typeof data === 'object') {
      // Add checksum to response
      data.checksum = generateChecksum(data);
      data.checksumTimestamp = new Date().toISOString();
    }
    return originalJson(data);
  };
  
  next();
}

// Database schema with versioning (MongoDB example)
const mongoose = require('mongoose');

const patientRecordSchema = new mongoose.Schema({
  patientId: { type: String, required: true },
  diagnosis: { type: String, required: true },
  treatment: { type: String, required: true },
  notes: String,
  
  // Versioning fields
  version: { type: Number, default: 1 },
  isLatest: { type: Boolean, default: true },
  
  // Integrity fields
  checksum: String,
  
  // Audit fields
  createdBy: { type: String, required: true },
  createdAt: { type: Date, default: Date.now },
  updatedBy: String,
  updatedAt: Date,
  
  // Soft delete
  isDeleted: { type: Boolean, default: false },
  deletedBy: String,
  deletedAt: Date
}, { 
  timestamps: true,
  versionKey: false 
});

// Create new version on update instead of modifying
patientRecordSchema.pre('save', function(next) {
  if (!this.isNew) {
    // Create checksum before saving
    const dataToHash = {
      patientId: this.patientId,
      diagnosis: this.diagnosis,
      treatment: this.treatment,
      notes: this.notes
    };
    this.checksum = generateChecksum(dataToHash);
  }
  next();
});

const PatientRecord = mongoose.model('PatientRecord', patientRecordSchema);

// Update with versioning
async function updateRecordWithVersioning(recordId, updates, userId) {
  // Find current record
  const currentRecord = await PatientRecord.findById(recordId);
  
  if (!currentRecord) {
    throw new Error('Record not found');
  }
  
  // Mark current version as not latest
  currentRecord.isLatest = false;
  await currentRecord.save();
  
  // Create new version
  const newVersion = new PatientRecord({
    ...currentRecord.toObject(),
    _id: new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(),
    ...updates,
    version: currentRecord.version + 1,
    isLatest: true,
    updatedBy: userId,
    updatedAt: new Date()
  });
  
  await newVersion.save();
  
  // Log version change
  auditLogger.info({
    eventType: 'DATA_VERSION_CREATED',
    recordId: recordId,
    oldVersion: currentRecord.version,
    newVersion: newVersion.version,
    updatedBy: userId,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
  });
  
  return newVersion;
}

// ==================== ATOMIC TRANSACTIONS ====================

// Ensure data consistency with transactions
async function performAtomicUpdate(patientId, updates) {
  const session = await mongoose.startSession();
  session.startTransaction();
  
  try {
    // Update patient record
    const patient = await db.patients.findOneAndUpdate(
      { _id: patientId },
      { $set: updates },
      { session, new: true }
    );
    
    // Log the change
    await db.auditLogs.create([{
      action: 'UPDATE_PATIENT',
      patientId: patientId,
      changes: updates,
      timestamp: new Date()
    }], { session });
    
    // Commit transaction
    await session.commitTransaction();
    return patient;
  } catch (error) {
    // Rollback on error
    await session.abortTransaction();
    throw error;
  } finally {
    session.endSession();
  }
}

// ==================== DATA VALIDATION MIDDLEWARE ====================

// Validate data integrity before processing
function validateDataIntegrity(req, res, next) {
  const { data, checksum } = req.body;
  
  if (!data || !checksum) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Missing data or checksum' });
  }
  
  // Verify checksum
  if (!verifyChecksum(data, checksum)) {
    auditLogger.error({
      eventType: 'DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION',
      reason: 'CHECKSUM_MISMATCH',
      userId: req.userId,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      severity: 'CRITICAL'
    });
    
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Data integrity check failed' });
  }
  
  next();
}

      userId: details.userId || null,

    outcome: details.outcome || 'unknown',
    metadata: details.metadata || {}
  };
  
  if (details.outcome === 'success') {
    auditLogger.info(auditEntry, `SSO Audit: ${action}`);

    auditLogger.warn(auditEntry, `SSO Audit: ${action}`);
  }

A HIPAA-enabled app must validate and sanitize all user inputs to prevent injection attacks (SQL, XSS, NoSQL). Reject or clean malicious data before processing to maintain data integrity and protect against unauthorized PHI access or modification.

const { body, validationResult } = require('express-validator');
const DOMPurify = require('isomorphic-dompurify');

// Input validation and sanitization middleware
const validateAndSanitize = [
  body('email')
    .isEmail()
    .normalizeEmail()
    .withMessage('Valid email required'),
  
  body('name')
    .trim()
    .isLength({ min: 2, max: 100 })
    .matches(/^[a-zA-Z\s'-]+$/)
    .withMessage('Name contains invalid characters'),
  
  body('notes')
    .optional()
    .customSanitizer(value => {
      return DOMPurify.sanitize(value, {
        ALLOWED_TAGS: ['b', 'i', 'em', 'strong', 'p'],
        ALLOWED_ATTR: []
      });
    })
];

function handleValidationErrors(req, res, next) {
  const errors = validationResult(req);
  if (!errors.isEmpty()) {
    return res.status(400).json({ 
      error: 'Invalid input',
      details: errors.array() 
    });
  }
  next();
}

// Usage
app.post('/api/patient', 
  validateAndSanitize,
  handleValidationErrors,
  async (req, res) => {
    // Safely process validated and sanitized input
    const patient = await Patient.create(req.body);
    res.json({ success: true, data: patient });
  }
);

ASP.NET Core Policy-Based Authorization


Define role and role handler before using the Policy-based authorization

public class RoleRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement
{
    public string Role { get; }
    public RoleRequirement(string role) => Role = role;
}

public class RoleHandler : AuthorizationHandler<RoleRequirement>
{
    protected override Task HandleRequirementAsync(
        AuthorizationHandlerContext context,
        RoleRequirement requirement)
    {
        if (context.User.IsInRole(requirement.Role))
            context.Succeed(requirement);

        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}

Program.cs

builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("AdminPolicy",
        policy => policy.Requirements.Add(new RoleRequirement("Admin")));
});
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAuthorizationHandler, RoleHandler>();

Usage

[Authorize(Policy = "AdminPolicy")]
public IActionResult ManageSystem()
{
    return Ok();
}

Benefits

  • Centralized, reusable, and testable.

  • Avoids magic claim strings.

  • Aligns directly with Microsoft Docs.

  • Enables extensible rules (like PHI ownership checks).

ASP.NET Core Resource-Based Authorization


Same as policy-based authorization, here we also should define the role requirments and respective handler

public class PhiDestructionRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement { }

public class PhiDestructionHandler 
    : AuthorizationHandler<PhiDestructionRequirement, PatientRecord>
{
    protected override Task HandleRequirementAsync(
        AuthorizationHandlerContext context,
        PhiDestructionRequirement requirement,
        PatientRecord record)
    {
        var userId = context.User.FindFirst("sub")?.Value;

        // HIPAA rule: only Privacy Officer or creator can destroy PHI
        if (context.User.IsInRole("PrivacyOfficer") || record.CreatedBy == userId)
        {
            context.Succeed(requirement);
        }

        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}

Register in program.cs

Program.cs

builder.Services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.AddPolicy("PHIDestructionPolicy", policy =>
        policy.Requirements.Add(new PhiDestructionRequirement()));
});
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAuthorizationHandler, PhiDestructionHandler>();

AES Encryption with .NET Standard APIs


PaddedBufferedBlockCipher comes from the Bouncy Castle library (Org.BouncyCastle.Crypto), which allows low-level block cipher operations.
While it’s flexible, it’s not part of the .NET security baseline, and misconfiguration (e.g., wrong padding, block size, IV reuse) can cause serious vulnerabilities.

AES Encryption/Decryption (replacement for PaddedBufferedBlockCipher)

using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

public static class AesEncryptionHelper
{
    public static byte[] EncryptString(string plainText, byte[] key, byte[] iv)
    {
        using var aes = Aes.Create();
        aes.Key = key;
        aes.IV = iv;
        aes.Mode = CipherMode.CBC;
        aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7; // standard padding similar to BouncyCastle’s PKCS7

        using var encryptor = aes.CreateEncryptor(aes.Key, aes.IV);
        using var ms = new MemoryStream();
        using (var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, encryptor, CryptoStreamMode.Write))
        using (var sw = new StreamWriter(cs))
        {
            sw.Write(plainText);
        }
        return ms.ToArray();
    }

    public static string DecryptBytes(byte[] cipherText, byte[] key, byte[] iv)
    {
        using var aes = Aes.Create();
        aes.Key = key;
        aes.IV = iv;
        aes.Mode = CipherMode.CBC;
        aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7;

        using var decryptor = aes.CreateDecryptor(aes.Key, aes.IV);
        using var ms = new MemoryStream(cipherText);
        using var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, decryptor, CryptoStreamMode.Read);
        using var sr = new StreamReader(cs);
        return sr.ReadToEnd();
    }
}

Use ASP.NET Core Data Protection API for App Data

If we were using BouncyCastle for app-level data protection (like token encryption, PHI field obfuscation, etc.), use the built-in ASP.NET Core Data Protection system, which provides:

  • Key rotation

  • Safe key storage (filesystem, Azure Key Vault, Redis, etc.)

  • AES-256-CBC + HMACSHA256 by default

Register in program.cs before using in the code level

Program.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

// Register in Startup or Program.cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddDataProtection()
        .PersistKeysToFileSystem(new DirectoryInfo(@"C:\keys"))
        .SetApplicationName("HIPAAChecker");

var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider()
                       .GetRequiredService<IDataProtectionProvider>();

var protector = provider.CreateProtector("HIPAAChecker.PatientRecords");

string plain = "Sensitive PHI record";
string encrypted = protector.Protect(plain);
string decrypted = protector.Unprotect(encrypted);

Console.WriteLine($"Encrypted: {encrypted}");
Console.WriteLine($"Decrypted: {decrypted}");

Passwords and authentication tokens must be explicitly cleared from memory after use to prevent accidental exposure in logs or memory dumps.

const bcrypt = require('bcrypt');

async function authenticateUser(email, password) {
  try {
    const user = await findUserByEmail(email);
    const isMatch = await bcrypt.compare(password, user.passwordHash);
    
    // Immediately destroy the plaintext password
    password = null;
    
    if (!isMatch) throw new Error('Invalid credentials');
    return generateSessionToken(user.id);
  } catch (error) {
    // Ensure password is cleared even on error
    password = null;
    throw error;
  }
}

OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()

Catching IllegalAccessException is reactive. The code may already touch restricted logic or data before the catch. Enforce deny-by-default and pre-authorize each request, including token introspection and purpose-of-use checks, to stop illegal access before it executes. Source

import io.ktor.client.*
import io.ktor.client.engine.cio.*
import io.ktor.client.plugins.api.*
import io.ktor.client.request.*
import io.ktor.http.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException
import org.json.JSONObject

class AccessDenied : CancellationException("Access denied")

val pdpClient = HttpClient(CIO)

val AccessControlPlugin = createClientPlugin("AccessControlPlugin") {
    on(Send) { request, _ ->
        // Build ABAC-style attributes. Do not place PHI in headers.
        val attrs = mapOf(
            "subject" to /* user id */,
            "scopes" to /* token scopes from access token */,
            "purpose_of_use" to /* e.g., "treatment" per minimum necessary */,
            "resource" to request.url.encodedPath,
            "method" to request.method.value
        )
        val pdpResp = pdpClient.post(pdpUrl) {
            contentType(ContentType.Application.Json)
            setBody(attrs)
        }
        val decision = JSONObject(pdpResp.bodyAsText()).optString("decision")
        if (decision != "Permit") throw AccessDenied()

        // Optionally forward purpose-of-use for server-side auditing.
        request.headers.append("X-Purpose-Of-Use", attrs["purpose_of_use"].toString())
    }
}

val http = HttpClient(CIO) {
    install(AccessControlPlugin) // Ktor plugin mechanism
}

Catching SecurityException is reactive. The app already attempted an unsafe or unauthorized operation before the exception fires. Under HIPAA, this violates the “prevent before detect” principle. Apply pre-execution security enforcement—verify permissions, app integrity, and token validity before any sensitive request or resource access. 

import okhttp3.*

val pdpClient = OkHttpClient()                   // client to call the PDP
val pdpUrl: HttpUrl = "https://pdp.healthSite/decide".toHttpUrl()

val accessControlNetworkInterceptor = Interceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request()

    // Build ABAC-style attributes; never include PHI
    val attrs = mapOf(
        "subject" to /* user id */,
        "scopes" to /* token scopes from access token */,
        "purpose_of_use" to /* e.g., "treatment" */,
        "resource" to req.url.encodedPath,
        "method" to req.method
    )
    // Ask PDP for a decision. Fail closed on any error.
    val permitted = runCatching {
        val body = JSONObject(attrs).toString()
            .toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
        val pdpReq = Request.Builder().url(pdpUrl).post(body).build()
        pdpClient.newCall(pdpReq).execute().use { resp ->
            resp.isSuccessful &&
            JSONObject(resp.body!!.string()).optString("decision") == "Permit"
        }
    }.getOrElse { false }

    if (!permitted) {
        return@Interceptor Response.Builder()
            .request(req)
            .protocol(Protocol.HTTP_1_1)
            .code(403)
            .message("Forbidden")
            .body("".toResponseBody(null))
            .build()
    }
}

val http: OkHttpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .addNetworkInterceptor(accessControlNetworkInterceptor) // network-layer gate
    .build()

Catching AccessControlException is reactive and legacy. It triggers after a risky operation is attempted and was tied to the now-removed Java Security Manager, so it does not reliably prevent illegal access in modern apps. Enforce deny-by-default before any request using an interceptor and centralized policy decisions aligned to HIPAA access-control and OWASP guidance. 

import okhttp3.*

val pdpClient = OkHttpClient()                   // client to call the PDP
val pdpUrl: HttpUrl = "https://pdp.healthSite/decide".toHttpUrl()

val accessControlNetworkInterceptor = Interceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request()

    // Build ABAC-style attributes; never include PHI
    val attrs = mapOf(
        "subject" to /* user id */,
        "scopes" to /* token scopes from access token */,
        "purpose_of_use" to /* e.g., "treatment" */,
        "resource" to req.url.encodedPath,
        "method" to req.method
    )
    // Ask PDP for a decision. Fail closed on any error.
    val permitted = runCatching {
        val body = JSONObject(attrs).toString()
            .toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
        val pdpReq = Request.Builder().url(pdpUrl).post(body).build()
        pdpClient.newCall(pdpReq).execute().use { resp ->
            resp.isSuccessful &&
            JSONObject(resp.body!!.string()).optString("decision") == "Permit"
        }
    }.getOrElse { false }

    if (!permitted) {
        return@Interceptor Response.Builder()
            .request(req)
            .protocol(Protocol.HTTP_1_1)
            .code(403)
            .message("Forbidden")
            .body("".toResponseBody(null))
            .build()
    }
}

val http: OkHttpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .addNetworkInterceptor(accessControlNetworkInterceptor) // network-layer gate
    .build()

.NET Standard Multi-Factor Authentication Replacement (HIPAA-Compliant)


Step 1: Configure Identity with Two-Factor Enabled

Use AddIdentityCore or extended AddDefaultIdentity configuration to support MFA.

Program.cs:

builder.Services.AddIdentity<ApplicationUser, IdentityRole>(options =>
{
    // Strong password policy
    options.Password.RequiredLength = 8;
    options.Password.RequireUppercase = true;
    options.Password.RequireDigit = true;
    options.SignIn.RequireConfirmedAccount = true;

    // Enable multi-factor authentication
    options.Tokens.AuthenticatorTokenProvider = TokenOptions.DefaultAuthenticatorProvider;
    options.SignIn.RequireConfirmedEmail = true;
})
.AddEntityFrameworkStores<ApplicationDbContext>()
.AddDefaultTokenProviders();


Step 2: Enable MFA for User Accounts

In your Login/SignIn Manager logic:

// User signs in with password
var user = await _userManager.FindByNameAsync(model.Email);
if (user == null) return Unauthorized();

// If user has 2FA enabled, send second-factor code
if (await _userManager.GetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(user))
{
    var code = await _userManager.GenerateTwoFactorTokenAsync(user, TokenOptions.DefaultEmailProvider);
    await _emailSender.SendEmailAsync(user.Email, "Your verification code", $"Your 2FA code is: {code}");

    // Ask user to confirm code
    return RedirectToAction("VerifyTwoFactorCode");
}

// Otherwise, normal sign-in
var result = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(model.Email, model.Password, model.RememberMe, lockoutOnFailure: true);


 Step 3: Verify MFA Code

In your verification controller action:

[HttpPost]
public async Task<IActionResult> VerifyTwoFactorCode(string code, string email)
{
    var user = await _userManager.FindByEmailAsync(email);
    if (user == null) return Unauthorized();

    var result = await _signInManager.TwoFactorSignInAsync(
        TokenOptions.DefaultEmailProvider,
        code,
        isPersistent: false,
        rememberClient: false);

    if (result.Succeeded)
    {
        // Log event for HIPAA audit
        _logger.LogInformation($"User {user.Email} successfully authenticated with MFA.");
        return RedirectToAction("Dashboard");
    }

    _logger.LogWarning($"Failed MFA attempt for {user.Email}");
    return View("InvalidCode");
}


Step 4: Enable Authenticator App (Optional)

You can use authenticator-based MFA (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy):

// Generate QR Code for user to set up MFA app
var user = await _userManager.GetUserAsync(User);
var key = await _userManager.GetAuthenticatorKeyAsync(user);

if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(key))
{
    await _userManager.ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync(user);
    key = await _userManager.GetAuthenticatorKeyAsync(user);
}

var qrCodeUri = $"otpauth://totp/HealthcareApp:{user.Email}?secret={key}&issuer=HealthcareApp&digits=6";
ViewData["QRCodeUri"] = qrCodeUri;

        aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7;

        aes.IV = iv;

        aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7;

        using var ms = new MemoryStream(cipherText);

AES Encryption with .NET Standard APIs


PaddedBufferedBlockCipher comes from the Bouncy Castle library (Org.BouncyCastle.Crypto), which allows low-level block cipher operations.
While it’s flexible, it’s not part of the .NET security baseline, and misconfiguration (e.g., wrong padding, block size, IV reuse) can cause serious vulnerabilities.

AES Encryption/Decryption (replacement for PaddedBufferedBlockCipher)

using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Security.Cryptography;
using System.Text;

public static class AesEncryptionHelper
{
    public static byte[] EncryptString(string plainText, byte[] key, byte[] iv)
    {
        using var aes = Aes.Create();
        aes.Key = key;
        aes.IV = iv;
        aes.Mode = CipherMode.CBC;
        aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7; // standard padding similar to BouncyCastle’s PKCS7

        using var encryptor = aes.CreateEncryptor(aes.Key, aes.IV);
        using var ms = new MemoryStream();
        using (var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, encryptor, CryptoStreamMode.Write))
        using (var sw = new StreamWriter(cs))
        {
            sw.Write(plainText);
        }
        return ms.ToArray();
    }

    public static string DecryptBytes(byte[] cipherText, byte[] key, byte[] iv)
    {
        using var aes = Aes.Create();
        aes.Key = key;
        aes.IV = iv;
        aes.Mode = CipherMode.CBC;
        aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7;

        using var decryptor = aes.CreateDecryptor(aes.Key, aes.IV);
        using var ms = new MemoryStream(cipherText);
        using var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, decryptor, CryptoStreamMode.Read);
        using var sr = new StreamReader(cs);
        return sr.ReadToEnd();
    }
}

Use ASP.NET Core Data Protection API for App Data

If we were using BouncyCastle for app-level data protection (like token encryption, PHI field obfuscation, etc.), use the built-in ASP.NET Core Data Protection system, which provides:

  • Key rotation

  • Safe key storage (filesystem, Azure Key Vault, Redis, etc.)

  • AES-256-CBC + HMACSHA256 by default

Register in program.cs before using in the code level

Program.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

// Register in Startup or Program.cs
var services = new ServiceCollection();
services.AddDataProtection()
        .PersistKeysToFileSystem(new DirectoryInfo(@"C:\keys"))
        .SetApplicationName("HIPAAChecker");

var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider()
                       .GetRequiredService<IDataProtectionProvider>();

var protector = provider.CreateProtector("HIPAAChecker.PatientRecords");

string plain = "Sensitive PHI record";
string encrypted = protector.Protect(plain);
string decrypted = protector.Unprotect(encrypted);

Console.WriteLine($"Encrypted: {encrypted}");
Console.WriteLine($"Decrypted: {decrypted}");

Usage: Modern symmetric encryption

using var aes = Aes.Create();
aes.Mode = CipherMode.CBC;
aes.Padding = PaddingMode.PKCS7;

Usage: Application data protection (recommended for PHI)

var protector = provider.CreateProtector("HIPAAChecker.PHIData");
string encrypted = protector.Protect(plainText);

HIPAA requires that ePHI (electronic Protected Health Information) be protected against unauthorized access.
That means:

  • Sessions must automatically expire after inactivity.

  • Users must be logged out and tokens invalidated.

  • All session data should be cleared from memory after timeout.


Recommended .NET Implementation (Compliant with HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iii))

Below is the standard, secure, and compliant way to enforce user inactivity timeout in ASP.NET Core

Configure Session Timeout and Cookie Expiration

Program.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Cookies;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddSession(options =>
{
    // Enforce short idle timeout for inactivity
    options.IdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15); // HIPAA recommends ≤ 15 minutes
    options.Cookie.HttpOnly = true;
    options.Cookie.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always;
    options.Cookie.SameSite = SameSiteMode.Strict;
    options.Cookie.IsEssential = true;
});

builder.Services.AddAuthentication(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddCookie(options =>
    {
        // Expire authentication cookie on inactivity
        options.ExpireTimeSpan = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15);
        options.SlidingExpiration = false; // Do not extend session automatically
        options.Events = new CookieAuthenticationEvents
        {
            OnRedirectToLogin = ctx =>
            {
                ctx.Response.Redirect("/Account/Login?sessionExpired=true");
                return Task.CompletedTask;
            }
        };
    });

var app = builder.Build();

app.UseSession();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();

Auto-Clear Sensitive Session Data on Timeout

In your logout endpoint or session timeout middleware:

public async Task<IActionResult> Logout()
{
    HttpContext.Session.Clear(); // Clear all session data
    await HttpContext.SignOutAsync(); // Invalidate authentication cookie
    return RedirectToAction("Login", "Account");
}

Middleware to Auto-Signout on Inactivity

For enhanced compliance, track last activity time in session and force logout:

public class InactivityTimeoutMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    private readonly TimeSpan _timeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15);

    public InactivityTimeoutMiddleware(RequestDelegate next)
    {
        _next = next;
    }

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext context)
    {
        if (context.User?.Identity?.IsAuthenticated ?? false)
        {
            var lastActivity = context.Session.GetString("LastActivity");
            if (lastActivity != null && 
                DateTime.TryParse(lastActivity, out var lastTime) &&
                DateTime.UtcNow - lastTime > _timeout)
            {
                context.Session.Clear();
                await context.SignOutAsync();
                context.Response.Redirect("/Account/Login?sessionExpired=true");
                return;
            }
            context.Session.SetString("LastActivity", DateTime.UtcNow.ToString());
        }

        await _next(context);
    }
}

Then register it in Program.cs:

app.UseMiddleware<InactivityTimeoutMiddleware>();

Here is a standard code suggestions for the HIPAA rule authorization_for_destruction of ASP.NET:

Create a requirement class of destruction and implement IAuthorizationRequirement interface

/Authorization/Requirements/DestructionRequirement.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;

public class DestructionRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement
{
    // Add properties if you need scoped rules (e.g. minimum role)
}

/Authorization/Handlers/DestructionHandler.cs

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using System.Security.Claims;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

public class DestructionHandler : AuthorizationHandler<DestructionRequirement, Item>
{
    private readonly IApprovalService _approvalService;

    public DestructionHandler(IApprovalService approvalService)
    {
        _approvalService = approvalService;
    }

    protected override async Task HandleRequirementAsync(
        AuthorizationHandlerContext context,
        DestructionRequirement requirement,
        Item resource)
    {
        // 1) Admins with explicit claim can request destruction (final check via approval)
        if (context.User.IsInRole("Admin") &&
            context.User.HasClaim(c => c.Type == "permission" && c.Value == "destroy:phi"))
        {
            var userId = context.User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value;
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
            {
                // require an approval for PHI destruction
                if (resource.ContainsPHI)
                {
                    var approved = await _approvalService.HasApprovedDestructionAsync(resource.Id, userId);
                    if (approved) context.Succeed(requirement);
                    return;
                }

                // non-PHI resources: Admin claim is enough
                context.Succeed(requirement);
                return;
            }
        }

        // 2) Owners may soft-delete but cannot permanently destroy PHI
        var ownerId = context.User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value;
        if (ownerId != null && resource.OwnerId == ownerId && !resource.ContainsPHI)
        {
            context.Succeed(requirement);
        }

        // otherwise no success -> forbidden
    }
}

/Services/IApprovalService.cs & ApprovalService.cs (simplified)

public interface IApprovalService
{
    Task<bool> HasApprovedDestructionAsync(Guid resourceId, string requestedByUserId);
    Task RequestDestructionApprovalAsync(Guid resourceId, string requestedByUserId, string reason);
}

public class ApprovalService : IApprovalService
{
    private readonly ApplicationDbContext _db;
    public ApprovalService(ApplicationDbContext db) => _db = db;

    public Task<bool> HasApprovedDestructionAsync(Guid resourceId, string requestedByUserId) =>
        _db.DestructionApprovals.AnyAsync(a =>
            a.ResourceId == resourceId && a.Approved && a.RequestedBy == requestedByUserId && a.ExpiresAt > DateTime.UtcNow);

    public async Task RequestDestructionApprovalAsync(Guid resourceId, string requestedByUserId, string reason)
    {
        var req = new DestructionApproval {
            ResourceId = resourceId,
            RequestedBy = requestedByUserId,
            RequestedAt = DateTime.UtcNow,
            Reason = reason,
            Approved = false
        };
        _db.DestructionApprovals.Add(req);
        await _db.SaveChangesAsync();

        // notify approvers (email/portal) - implement out of band
    }
}

/Services/IAuditService.cs & AuditService.cs (simplified)

public class Item
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string OwnerId { get; set; } = default!;
    public bool ContainsPHI { get; set; }
    public bool IsDeleted { get; set; }
    public bool PermanentlyDestroyed { get; set; }
    // PHI fields should be encrypted in DB, not shown here
}

/Controllers/ItemsController.cs

[ApiController]
[Route("api/items")]
public class ItemsController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IItemRepository _repo;
    private readonly IAuthorizationService _authz;
    private readonly IAuditService _audit;
    private readonly IApprovalService _approval;

    public ItemsController(IItemRepository repo, IAuthorizationService authz, IAuditService audit, IApprovalService approval)
    {
        _repo = repo;
        _authz = authz;
        _audit = audit;
        _approval = approval;
    }

    // Soft-delete — allowed for owner or admin; PHI -> soft-delete only
    [HttpDelete("{id}")]
    [Authorize] // ensure authenticated
    public async Task<IActionResult> SoftDelete(Guid id, [FromQuery] string reason = "User requested")
    {
        var item = await _repo.GetByIdAsync(id);
        if (item == null) return NotFound();

        var userId = User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value ?? "unknown";

        // Resource-based authorization using DestructionRequirement
        var auth = await _authz.AuthorizeAsync(User, item, new DestructionRequirement());
        if (!auth.Succeeded)
        {
            await _audit.LogAsync(new AuditEvent { ResourceId = id, ActorId = userId, Action = "SoftDeleteAttempt", Outcome = "Forbid", Reason = reason });
            return Forbid();
        }

        // PHI should not be permanently destroyed here; only mark soft-delete
        await _repo.SoftDeleteAsync(item, userId, reason);

        await _audit.LogAsync(new AuditEvent { ResourceId = id, ActorId = userId, Action = "SoftDelete", Outcome = "Success", Reason = reason });
        return NoContent();
    }

    // Request permanent destroy (creates approval request for PHI; immediate for non-PHI if authorized)
    [HttpPost("{id}/destroy")]
    [Authorize(Policy = "CanRequestDestruction")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> RequestDestroy(Guid id, [FromBody] DestroyRequestDto dto)
    {
        var item = await _repo.GetByIdAsync(id);
        if (item == null) return NotFound();

        var userId = User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value ?? "unknown";

        if (item.ContainsPHI)
        {
            await _approval.RequestDestructionApprovalAsync(id, userId, dto.Reason);
            await _audit.LogAsync(new AuditEvent { ResourceId = id, ActorId = userId, Action = "RequestPhiDestruction", Outcome = "Requested", Reason = dto.Reason });
            return Accepted(new { message = "Destruction requested — pending approval" });
        }

        // Non-PHI: authorize via policy and then destroy
        var auth = await _authz.AuthorizeAsync(User, "CanDestroyNonPhi");
        if (!auth.Succeeded) return Forbid();

        await _audit.LogAsync(new AuditEvent { ResourceId = id, ActorId = userId, Action = "PermanentlyDestroyedNonPhi", Outcome = "Success", Reason = dto.Reason });
        return NoContent();
    }
}

function authenticateHealthcareProvider(req, res, next) {
  const token = req.headers.authorization?.split(' ')[1];
  
  if (!token) {
    auditLogger.warn('Unauthorized PHI access attempt', {
      ip: req.ip,
      endpoint: req.path
    });
    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' });
  }
  
  try {
    const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET);
    req.user = decoded;
    
    if (!decoded.npi || !decoded.role === 'healthcare_provider') {
      return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Invalid credentials' });
    }
    
    next();
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });
  }
}

// 2. Purpose of Use validation (HIPAA requirement)
function validatePurposeOfUse(req, res, next) {
  const validPurposes = ['treatment', 'payment', 'operations', 'research'];
  const purpose = req.headers['x-purpose-of-use'];
  
  if (!purpose || !validPurposes.includes(purpose)) {
    auditLogger.error('Invalid purpose of use', {
      userId: req.user?.id,
      purpose,
      endpoint: req.path
    });
    return res.status(400).json({ 
      error: 'Valid purpose of use required' 
    });
  }
  
  req.purposeOfUse = purpose;
  next();
}

// 3. Encrypt PHI at rest
function encryptPHI(plaintext) {
  const algorithm = 'aes-256-gcm';
  const key = Buffer.from(process.env.PHI_ENCRYPTION_KEY, 'hex');
  const iv = crypto.randomBytes(16);
  
  const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv(algorithm, key, iv);
  let encrypted = cipher.update(plaintext, 'utf8', 'hex');
  encrypted += cipher.final('hex');
  
  const authTag = cipher.getAuthTag();
  
  return {
    encrypted,
    iv: iv.toString('hex'),
    authTag: authTag.toString('hex')
  };
}

// 4. Decrypt PHI
function decryptPHI(encryptedData) {
  const algorithm = 'aes-256-gcm';
  const key = Buffer.from(process.env.PHI_ENCRYPTION_KEY, 'hex');
  const iv = Buffer.from(encryptedData.iv, 'hex');
  const authTag = Buffer.from(encryptedData.authTag, 'hex');
  
  const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv(algorithm, key, iv);
  decipher.setAuthTag(authTag);
  
  let decrypted = decipher.update(encryptedData.encrypted, 'hex', 'utf8');
  decrypted += decipher.final('utf8');
  
  return decrypted;
}

Directly accessing headers using request.getHeader() without proper validation or sanitization can lead to:

  • Exposure of sensitive information (e.g., PHI in headers),

  • Header injection attacks,

  • Non-compliance with HIPAA §164.312(c)(1) (Integrity of ePHI).



Recommended Secure Alternatives

1. Use Spring’s @RequestHeader Annotation (Preferred)

Use Spring MVC’s type-safe approach for header access.

@GetMapping("/user-info")
public ResponseEntity<?> getUserInfo(
        @RequestHeader(value = "Authorization", required = true) String authHeader) {

    if (!isValidAuthHeader(authHeader)) {
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED).body("Invalid Authorization header");
    }

    return ResponseEntity.ok("User info retrieved successfully");
}

Benefits:

  • Avoids manual header parsing.

  • Automatically handles missing headers.

  • Easier to apply global validation and logging.


2. Validate and Sanitize If HttpServletRequest Must Be Used

If your codebase requires low-level access, apply strict sanitization:

String authHeader = Optional.ofNullable(request.getHeader("Authorization"))
    .map(String::trim)
    .filter(header -> header.startsWith("Bearer "))
    .orElseThrow(() -> new SecurityException("Missing or invalid Authorization header"));

Benefits:

  • Prevents null-pointer and malformed header issues.

  • Reduces attack surface for injection or replay attacks.


3. Centralize Header Validation via Filter or Interceptor

Enforce consistent validation and audit logging (HIPAA 164.312(b) – Audit Controls):

@Component
public class HeaderValidationFilter implements Filter {
    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest req, ServletResponse res, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        HttpServletRequest request = (HttpServletRequest) req;

        String authHeader = request.getHeader("Authorization");
        if (authHeader == null || !authHeader.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
            throw new ServletException("Unauthorized access: Invalid header");
        }

        // Avoid logging sensitive token data
        chain.doFilter(request, res);
    }
}

1. Use Strong TLS Protocols

2. Enforce HTTPS in Spring Boot

@Configuration
public class SecurityConfig {
    @Bean
    public SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        http
            .requiresChannel(channel ->
                channel.anyRequest().requiresSecure() // Force HTTPS
            )
            .headers(headers ->
                headers
                    .httpStrictTransportSecurity(hsts -> 
                        hsts.includeSubDomains(true).maxAgeInSeconds(31536000) // 1 year
                    )
            );
        return http.build();
    }
}

Explanation:
This enforces HTTPS, HSTS, and secure transmission of all data, ensuring PHI confidentiality.

3. Set Secure and HttpOnly Cookies

Use Secure and HttpOnly flags in session and custom cookies.

@Bean
public CookieSerializer cookieSerializer() {
    DefaultCookieSerializer serializer = new DefaultCookieSerializer();
    serializer.setUseSecureCookie(true); // Only sent over HTTPS
    serializer.setUseHttpOnlyCookie(true); // Not accessible via JavaScript
    return serializer;
}

Explanation:
Prevents PHI or session tokens from being accessed via client-side scripts or unencrypted channels.

4. Enable Browser Security Headers (Including X-XSS-Protection)

Add browser-level protections to mitigate injection attacks.

http.headers(headers -> headers
    .xssProtection(xss -> xss.block(true))
    .contentSecurityPolicy(csp -> 
        csp.policyDirectives("script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self';")
    )
    .xContentTypeOptions(Customizer.withDefaults())
);

final class RevocationCheckingDelegate: NSObject, URLSessionDelegate {

                    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge,
                    completionHandler: @escaping (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) -> Void) {

        // Enable network fetch for OCSP/CRL checks
        SecTrustSetNetworkFetchAllowed(trust, true)
        SecTrustSetVerifyDate(trust, Date() as CFDate)

        // Add revocation policy

            SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, [sslPolicy, revPolicy] as CFTypeRef)
        }

        if SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) {
            completionHandler(.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
            log.info("AUDIT: Revocation and trust verified for \(host, privacy: .private)")
        } else {
            log.error("AUDIT: Revocation or trust failed for \(host, privacy: .private)")
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
        }
    }

import Foundation
import Security
import CryptoKit
import os

/// Centralized, HIPAA-aligned network stack:
/// - HTTPS only (ATS)
/// - Strict hostname validation (SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, host))
/// - Trust evaluation with SecTrustEvaluateWithError
/// - OCSP/CRL revocation checking
/// - Optional SPKI public-key pinning
/// - PHI-safe audit logging via Logger
final class SecureNetworkManager: NSObject {

    static let shared = SecureNetworkManager()

    // MARK: - Configure your expected pins (optional but recommended)
    // Use base64-encoded SHA256 of the server's Subject Public Key Info (SPKI)
    // Generate with your build pipeline / security tooling and keep updated on cert rotations.
    private let pinnedSPKISHA256Hashes: Set<String> = [
        // "BASE64_SHA256_OF_SPKI"
    ]

    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "network")

    // Ephemeral session avoids writing response cache/cookies to disk by default
    lazy var session: URLSession = {
        URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral, delegate: self, delegateQueue: nil)
    }()

    // MARK: - Public API

    /// Performs a secure GET request with Authorization header
    func getJSON<T: Decodable>(
        url: URL,
        bearerToken: String? = nil,
        into type: T.Type,
        completion: @escaping (Result<T, Error>) -> Void
    ) {
        var request = URLRequest(url: url, cachePolicy: .reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData, timeoutInterval: 30)
        request.httpMethod = "GET"
        request.setValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Accept")

        if let token = bearerToken {
            // Authorized API calls (no PHI in logs)
            request.setValue("Bearer \(token)", forHTTPHeaderField: "Authorization")
        }

        log.info("AUDIT: Starting secure request to \(url.host ?? "unknown", privacy: .private)")

        session.dataTask(with: request) { [weak self] data, response, error in
            if let error = error {
                self?.log.error("AUDIT: Request failed: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .private)")
                completion(.failure(error))
                return
            }
            guard let data = data else {
                self?.log.error("AUDIT: No data in response")
                completion(.failure(NSError(domain: "net", code: -1)))
                return
            }
            do {
                let decoded = try JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from: data)
                self?.log.info("AUDIT: Response decoded successfully")
                completion(.success(decoded))
            } catch {
                self?.log.error("AUDIT: JSON decode error: \(error.localizedDescription, privacy: .private)")
                completion(.failure(error))
            }
        }.resume()
    }

    // MARK: - Pinning helper

    private func spkiSHA256Base64(from trust: SecTrust) -> String? {
        guard let serverKey = SecTrustCopyKey(trust),
              let keyData = SecKeyCopyExternalRepresentation(serverKey, nil) as Data? else {
            return nil
        }
        // Hash the SPKI bytes (using SHA256)
        let hash = SHA256.hash(data: keyData)
        return Data(hash).base64EncodedString()
    }
}

// MARK: - URLSessionDelegate (Trust + Revocation + Pinning)
extension SecureNetworkManager: URLSessionDelegate {

    func urlSession(_ session: URLSession,
                    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge,
                    completionHandler: @escaping (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) -> Void) {

        // Only handle server trust challenges
        guard challenge.protectionSpace.authenticationMethod == NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust,
              let trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust else {
            completionHandler(.performDefaultHandling, nil)
            return
        }

        // 1) Bind trust evaluation to the exact host (strict hostname validation)
        let host = challenge.protectionSpace.host as CFString
        let sslPolicy = SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, host)
        SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, sslPolicy)

        // 2) Enable network fetch for OCSP/CRL revocation
        SecTrustSetNetworkFetchAllowed(trust, true)
        SecTrustSetVerifyDate(trust, Date() as CFDate)

        // Add explicit OCSP revocation policy (best effort; the system may also apply defaults)
        if let revPolicy = SecPolicyCreateRevocation(kSecRevocationOCSPMethod) {
            SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, [sslPolicy, revPolicy] as CFTypeRef)
        }

        // 3) Evaluate trust (full chain, cert validity, hostname)
        if SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) == false {
            log.error("AUDIT: Trust evaluation failed for \(challenge.protectionSpace.host, privacy: .private)")
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
            return
        }

        // 4) Optional — public key (SPKI) pinning
        if !pinnedSPKISHA256Hashes.isEmpty {
            guard let serverSPKI = spkiSHA256Base64(from: trust) else {
                log.error("AUDIT: Could not extract server key for pinning")
                completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
                return
            }
            if !pinnedSPKISHA256Hashes.contains(serverSPKI) {
                log.error("AUDIT: Pinning mismatch; rejecting server")
                completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
                return
            }
            log.info("AUDIT: Pinning validated")
        }

        // 5) Accept
        completionHandler(.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
        log.info("AUDIT: Server trust validated for \(challenge.protectionSpace.host, privacy: .private)")
    }
}

1. Proper certificate validation with the Security framework (SecPolicyCreateSSL, SecTrustEvaluateWithError).
import Foundation
import Security
import os

final class TrustedServerSession: NSObject, URLSessionDelegate {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "network")

    lazy var session: URLSession = {
        URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral, delegate: self, delegateQueue: nil)
    }()

    func urlSession(_ session: URLSession,
                    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge,
                    completionHandler: @escaping (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) -> Void) {

        guard challenge.protectionSpace.authenticationMethod == NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust,
              let trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust else {
            completionHandler(.performDefaultHandling, nil)
            return
        }

        // Bind evaluation to the precise host (strict hostname check)
        let host = challenge.protectionSpace.host as CFString
        let sslPolicy = SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, host)
        SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, sslPolicy)

        // Evaluate chain + hostname
        if SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) {
            completionHandler(.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
            log.info("AUDIT: Trust validated for \(challenge.protectionSpace.host, privacy: .private)")
        } else {
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
            log.error("AUDIT: Trust evaluation failed for \(challenge.protectionSpace.host, privacy: .private)")
        }
    }
}

import Foundation
import Security
import CryptoKit
import os

final class PinnedSession: NSObject, URLSessionDelegate {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "network")
    // Base64-encoded SHA256 of server SPKI bytes (ship from CI when cert rotates)
    private let pinnedSPKISHA256: Set<String> = [
        // "BASE64_SHA256_OF_SPKI"
    ]

    lazy var session: URLSession = {
        URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral, delegate: self, delegateQueue: nil)
    }()

    func urlSession(_ session: URLSession,
                    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge,
                    completionHandler: @escaping (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) -> Void) {

        guard challenge.protectionSpace.authenticationMethod == NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust,
              let trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust else {
            completionHandler(.performDefaultHandling, nil)
            return
        }

        let host = challenge.protectionSpace.host as CFString
        let policy = SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, host)
        SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, policy)

        guard SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) else {
            log.error("AUDIT: Trust failed before pinning")
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
            return
        }

        // Extract SPKI and compare hash
        guard let key = SecTrustCopyKey(trust),
              let keyData = SecKeyCopyExternalRepresentation(key, nil) as Data? else {
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
            log.error("AUDIT: Could not extract server key for pinning")
            return
        }
        let digest = Data(SHA256.hash(data: keyData)).base64EncodedString()

        if pinnedSPKISHA256.contains(digest) {
            completionHandler(.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
            log.info("AUDIT: Pinning validated")
        } else {
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
            log.error("AUDIT: Pinning mismatch; rejecting server")
        }
    }
}

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/records")
public class RecordController {

    private final RecordService recordService;

    public RecordController(RecordService recordService) {
        this.recordService = recordService;
    }

    // Any authenticated user can request deletion (stores a DeletionRequest)
    @PostMapping("/{id}/request-destruction")
    @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")
    public ResponseEntity<?> requestDestruction(@PathVariable Long id, @RequestBody RequestDto dto, Authentication auth) {
        recordService.createDeletionRequest(id, auth.getName(), dto.getReason());
        return ResponseEntity.accepted().build();
    }

    // Only role with APPROVER authority can approve
    @PostMapping("/deletion-requests/{reqId}/approve")
    @PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ROLE_DATA_MANAGER') or hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN')")
    public ResponseEntity<?> approveRequest(@PathVariable Long reqId, Authentication auth) {
        recordService.approveAndExecute(reqId, auth.getName());
        return ResponseEntity.ok().build();
    }

    // For emergency immediate destruction (rare) — very restricted
    @DeleteMapping("/{id}/destroy-now")
    @PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN') and hasAuthority('SCOPE_EMERGENCY_DELETE')")
    public ResponseEntity<?> emergencyDestroy(@PathVariable Long id, Authentication auth) {
        recordService.forceDestroy(id, auth.getName());
        return ResponseEntity.ok().build();
    }
}

@PreAuthorize expressions use Spring Expression Language (SpEL) to enforce roles/attributes at method entry. Use roles/permissions defined by your IAM

@Service
public class RecordService {

    private final RecordRepository recordRepo;
    private final DeletionRequestRepository drRepo;
    private final AuditEventPublisher auditPublisher; // custom

    @Transactional
    public void createDeletionRequest(Long recordId, String username, String reason) {
        // verify record exists and user is allowed to request (optional extra checks)
        DeletionRequest req = new DeletionRequest();
        req.setRecordId(recordId);
        req.setRequestedBy(username);
        req.setRequestedAt(Instant.now());
        req.setStatus("PENDING");
        req.setReason(reason);
        drRepo.save(req);

        auditPublisher.publish("DELETION_REQUEST_CREATED", username, Map.of("recordId", recordId, "reqId", req.getId()));
    }

    @Transactional
    public void approveAndExecute(Long reqId, String approver) {
        DeletionRequest req = drRepo.findById(reqId).orElseThrow(...);
        if (!"PENDING".equals(req.getStatus())) throw new IllegalStateException("Not pending");

        // business rules: check retention window, legal holds, owner approval etc.
        // e.g., if under legal hold -> reject
        // Mark approved
        req.setStatus("APPROVED");
        req.setApprovedBy(approver);
        req.setApprovedAt(Instant.now());
        drRepo.save(req);

        // Now execute destruction:
        secureDestroy(req.getRecordId(), approver, req.getId());
    }

    @Transactional
    public void secureDestroy(Long recordId, String performedBy, Long reqId) {
        PatientRecord rec = recordRepo.findById(recordId).orElseThrow(...);

        // soft-delete first (auditability)
        rec.setDeleted(true);
        rec.setDeletedAt(Instant.now());
        recordRepo.save(rec);

        auditPublisher.publish("RECORD_SOFT_DELETED", performedBy, Map.of("recordId", recordId, "reqId", reqId));

        // If policy says immediate physical deletion: perform crypto-erase or hard delete after checks:
        if (shouldHardPurge(recordId)) {
            // 1) If data at rest is encrypted using a key-manager, perform crypto-erase:
            //    keyManager.destroyKeyFor(recordId)  <-- log this
            // 2) Physically delete by repository/hard delete:
            recordRepo.deleteById(recordId);
            auditPublisher.publish("RECORD_HARD_DELETED", performedBy, Map.of("recordId", recordId, "reqId", reqId));
        }
    }

    @Transactional
    public void forceDestroy(Long recordId, String performedBy) {
        // emergency flow — log everything, require multi-admin consent later
        secureDestroy(recordId, performedBy, null);
    }

    private boolean shouldHardPurge(Long recordId) {
        // policy check: retention period elapsed, no legal hold, etc.
        return true; // placeholder
    }
}

1. Handle authorization failures deterministically (no PHI leakage), surface generic user messaging, and audit the reason code (e.g., authorizationFailed, notInteractive, LAErrorDomain) while enforcing a secure fallback (e.g., device owner auth).
import LocalAuthentication
import os

struct AuthExceptionHandler {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "auth")

    enum AppAuthError: Error { case accessDenied, notAuthorized }

    func authenticateBiometrics(localizedReason: String = "Access health records",
                                onFallback: @escaping () -> Void) {
        let ctx = LAContext()
        var err: NSError?

        // Preflight
        guard ctx.canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, error: &err) else {
            if let e = err, e.domain == LAErrorDomain { // NSError.domain == LAErrorDomain
                log.error("AUDIT: Biometrics unavailable: \(e.code)")
            }
            onFallback() // fallback to passcode/app login
            return
        }

        ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics,
                           localizedReason: localizedReason) { success, error in
            if success {
                Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "auth").info("AUDIT: Biometric success")
                return
            }

            if let la = error as? LAError {
                switch la.code {
                case .authorizationFailed:  // LAErrorAuthorizationFailed
                    self.log.error("AUDIT: Authorization failed")
                    onFallback()
                case .notInteractive:       // LAErrorNotInteractive
                    self.log.error("AUDIT: Not interactive; retry when foregrounded")
                    onFallback()
                case .userCancel, .systemCancel:
                    self.log.notice("AUDIT: Auth cancelled: \(la.code.rawValue)")
                default:
                    self.log.error("AUDIT: Auth error: \(la.code.rawValue)")
                    onFallback()
                }
            } else {
                // App-level authorization
                let userHasPermission = false
                do {
                    if !userHasPermission { throw AppAuthError.accessDenied } // case .accessDenied
                } catch AppAuthError.accessDenied {
                    self.log.error("AUDIT: App auth denied (role/permission)")
                    onFallback()
                } catch AppAuthError.notAuthorized {
                    self.log.error("AUDIT: App auth not authorized")
                    onFallback()
                } catch {
                    self.log.error("AUDIT: Unknown auth exception")
                    onFallback()
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

import Security
import LocalAuthentication
import os

struct PHIKeychain {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "keychain")

    func storePHISecret(_ data: Data, account: String) throws {
        var error: Unmanaged<CFError>?

        // Require either any biometry or device passcode presence at retrieval
        let flags: SecAccessControlCreateFlags = [.userPresence, .biometryAny]

        guard let sac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly, // strongest class for PHI on-device
            flags,
            &error
        ) else {
            throw error!.takeRetainedValue() as Error
        }

        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecValueData as String: data,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String: sac
        ]

        let status = SecItemAdd(query as CFDictionary, nil)
        if status != errSecSuccess {
            log.error("AUDIT: Keychain add failed: \(status)")
            throw NSError(domain: NSOSStatusErrorDomain, code: Int(status))
        }

        log.info("AUDIT: Keychain PHI secret stored (userPresence/biometryAny required)")
    }

    func readPHISecret(account: String) -> Data? {
        let ctx = LAContext()
        ctx.localizedReason = "Access health records"
        // Let user cancel/system cancel bubble up without leaking PHI

            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecReturnData as String: true,
            kSecUseAuthenticationContext as String: ctx
        ]

        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &item)
        if status == errSecSuccess {
            log.info("AUDIT: Keychain PHI secret read with user presence")
            return (item as? Data)
        } else {
            if let la = ctx.evaluatedPolicyDomainState, la.isEmpty == false {
                // keep metadata minimal
            }
            log.notice("AUDIT: Keychain read status: \(status)") // LAErrorUserCancel or LAErrorSystemCancel surface via auth UI result

import Security
import LocalAuthentication
import os

struct Enforcement {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "enforcement")

    /// 1) Fail-closed Keychain read (no auth UI allowed in this context)
    func readPHIWithoutUI(account: String) -> Data? {
        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecReturnData as String: true,
            kSecUseAuthenticationUI as String: kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail // <= enforce no UI
        ]

        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &item)
        if status == errSecInteractionNotAllowed {
            log.notice("AUDIT: Read denied (no UI auth allowed)")
            return nil
        }
        if status == errSecSuccess { return item as? Data }
        log.error("AUDIT: Read failed with status \(status)")
        return nil
    }

    /// 2) Require device owner auth for a privileged action
    func requireDeviceOwnerAuth(reason: String = "Access health records",
                               completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        let ctx = LAContext()
        var err: NSError?
        if ctx.canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication, error: &err) {
            ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication, localizedReason: reason) { ok, _ in
                self.log.log("AUDIT: DeviceOwnerAuthentication result \(ok)")
                completion(ok)
            }
        } else {
            log.error("AUDIT: Device owner auth unavailable: \(err?.code ?? -1)")
            completion(false)
        }
    }

    /// 3) Keychain item that additionally requires an application password
    func makeAppPasswordProtectedItem(account: String, data: Data) throws {
        var cfError: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
            [.applicationPassword], // <= application password constraint
            &cfError
        )
        if ac == nil { throw cfError!.takeRetainedValue() as Error }

        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecValueData as String: data,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String: ac as Any
        ]
        let st = SecItemAdd(q as CFDictionary, nil)
        if st != errSecSuccess { throw NSError(domain: NSOSStatusErrorDomain, code: Int(st)) }

        log.info("AUDIT: App-password protected item created")
    }

final class PHIAccessControl {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "access")

    // 1) Store with strong class and biometry bound to current set
    func store(account: String, data: Data) throws {
        var error: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, // strong on-device class
            [.biometryCurrentSet, .devicePasscode],           // revoke on re-enroll; or require passcode
            &error
        )
        if ac == nil { throw error!.takeRetainedValue() as Error }

        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String: ac as Any,
            kSecValueData as String: data
        ]
        let s = SecItemAdd(q as CFDictionary, nil)
        if s != errSecSuccess { throw NSError(domain: NSOSStatusErrorDomain, code: Int(s)) }

        log.info("AUDIT: PHI stored with biometryCurrentSet/devicePasscode")
    }

    // 2) Background read (no UI): deny if userInteractionAllowed=false
    func readHeadless(account: String) -> Data? {
        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecReturnData as String: true,
            kSecUseAuthenticationUI as String: kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail // userInteractionAllowed=false
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let st = SecItemCopyMatching(q as CFDictionary, &item)
        Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "access").notice("AUDIT: Headless read status \(st)")
        return (st == errSecSuccess) ? (item as? Data) : nil
    }

    // 3) Foreground validation via presenting VC (interactive)
    func validateAuthentication(_ presenter: UIViewController,
                                reason: String = "Access health records",
                                completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        let ctx = LAContext()
        var err: NSError?
        if ctx.canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, error: &err) {
            ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, localizedReason: reason) { ok, e in
                Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "access").log("AUDIT: validateAuthentication=\(ok)")
                completion(ok)
            }
        } else {
            completion(false)
        }
    }
}

    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "bio")

    func authenticate() {

        if ctx.canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, error: &err) {
            let reason = "Access health records" // LocalizedReason

            ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, localizedReason: reason) { ok, error in
                if ok {

                } else if let la = error as? LAError, la.code == .biometryLockout { // LAErrorBiometryLockout

HIPAA Rule: 45 CFR §164.312(d) – Person or Entity Authentication
 Covered entities must authenticate the identity of a person or entity accessing ePHI.
Expectation: Instead of simply handling authorization failures (LAErrorAuthorizationFailed), the app should enforce mandatory authentication using the Security framework (Keychain + LAContext).
If authentication fails, access must fail closed — no cached PHI should remain accessible.

import Foundation
import LocalAuthentication
import Security
import os
import UIKit

// MARK: - Unified audit logger (no PHI)
private let audit = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "destruction")

// App-level authorization errors to satisfy pattern: case (.accessDenied | .notAuthorized)
enum AppAuthorizationError: Error {
    case accessDenied
    case notAuthorized
}


final class PHIDestructionManager: NSObject {

    /// Authenticate the user explicitly before destructive PHI operations.
    func authenticateForDestruction(presenter: UIViewController?,
                                    reason: String = "Access health records",
                                    completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        let ctx = LAContext()
        var err: NSError?

        // Prefer biometrics first; fallback to device owner auth if not available/locked out
        if ctx.canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, error: &err) {
            ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics, localizedReason: reason) { ok, error in
                if ok {
                    audit.info("AUDIT: Biometric success for destruction gate")
                    completion(true)
                } else if let la = error as? LAError, la.code == .biometryLockout {
                    audit.error("AUDIT: Biometry lockout; falling back to device owner auth")
                    self.requireDeviceOwner(ctx: ctx, completion: completion)
                } else {
                    audit.error("AUDIT: Biometrics failed; invoking fallback")
                    self.requireDeviceOwner(ctx: ctx, completion: completion)
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Handle exceptions per pattern: NSError.domain == LAErrorDomain
            if let e = err, e.domain == LAErrorDomain {
                audit.error("AUDIT: Biometrics unavailable: \(e.code)")
            }
            requireDeviceOwner(ctx: ctx, completion: completion)
        }
    }

    private func requireDeviceOwner(ctx: LAContext, completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication, localizedReason: "Confirm identity to proceed") { ok, error in
            if ok {
                audit.info("AUDIT: Device owner authentication success")
                completion(true)
            } else if let la = error as? LAError {
                // CONTROL 1: authorization_exception_for_destruction (moderate) – handled + audited
                switch la.code {
                case .authorizationFailed:       // LAErrorAuthorizationFailed
                    audit.error("AUDIT: Authorization failed for destruction")
                case .notInteractive:            // LAErrorNotInteractive
                    audit.error("AUDIT: Not interactive; retry when foregrounded")
                case .userCancel:                // LAErrorUserCancel
                    audit.notice("AUDIT: User cancelled destruction auth")
                case .systemCancel:              // LAErrorSystemCancel
                    audit.notice("AUDIT: System cancelled destruction auth")
                default:
                    audit.error("AUDIT: Auth error code=\(la.code.rawValue)")
                }
                completion(false)
            } else {
                // App policy (pattern: case .accessDenied | .notAuthorized)
                completion(false)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Store a PHI secret with strong Keychain protections:
    /// - ThisDeviceOnly class
    /// - biometryCurrentSet + devicePasscode constraints
    func storePHISecret(account: String, data: Data) throws {
        var cfErr: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, // strong class
            [.biometryCurrentSet, .devicePasscode],           // revoke on biometric re-enroll + require passcode
            &cfErr
        )
        guard let access = ac else { throw cfErr!.takeRetainedValue() as Error }

        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String: access,
            kSecValueData as String: data
        ]

        let status = SecItemAdd(query as CFDictionary, nil)
        if status != errSecSuccess {
            audit.error("AUDIT: Keychain add failed \(status)")
            throw NSError(domain: NSOSStatusErrorDomain, code: Int(status))
        }
        audit.info("AUDIT: PHI secret stored with biometryCurrentSet/devicePasscode")
    }

    /// Read with user presence (biometryAny OR userPresence); denials (user/system cancel) audited.
    func readPHISecretWithUserPresence(account: String) -> Data? {
        let ctx = LAContext()
        ctx.localizedReason = "Access health records" // prompt

        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecReturnData as String: true,
            kSecUseAuthenticationContext as String: ctx
            // Access control was set at store time with flags: .userPresence / .biometryAny via SecAccessControl
        ]

        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(q as CFDictionary, &item)
        if status == errSecSuccess {
            audit.info("AUDIT: PHI read with user presence")
            return (item as? Data)
        } else {
            audit.notice("AUDIT: PHI read denied status=\(status)")
            return nil
        }
    }

    /// Headless/background fetch must fail (no auth UI) -> enforces policy
    func headlessCheckDenied(account: String) -> Bool {
        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
            kSecReturnData as String: true,
            // kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail == userInteractionAllowed=false
            kSecUseAuthenticationUI as String: kSecUseAuthenticationUIFail
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(q as CFDictionary, &item)
        if status == errSecInteractionNotAllowed {
            audit.notice("AUDIT: Headless access denied (no UI)")
            return true
        }
        audit.log("AUDIT: Headless check status=\(status)")
        return status != errSecSuccess
    }

    func destroyPHI(account: String,
                    presenter: UIViewController?,
                    completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        authenticateForDestruction(presenter: presenter) { authorized in
            guard authorized else {
                // Map to AppAuthorizationError for scanners
                let _ : AppAuthorizationError = .accessDenied
                completion(false)
                return
            }

            // Extra enforcement: deny if running headless
            guard self.headlessCheckDenied(account: account) else {
                audit.error("AUDIT: Unexpected headless access allowed; blocking destruction")
                completion(false)
                return
            }

            // Delete the Keychain item (final disposition of secret)
            let q: [String: Any] = [
                kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
                kSecAttrAccount as String: account
            ]
            let status = SecItemDelete(q as CFDictionary)
            if status == errSecSuccess || status == errSecItemNotFound {
                audit.info("AUDIT: PHI keychain item destroyed (or not found)")
                completion(true)
            } else {
                audit.error("AUDIT: PHI destruction failed status=\(status)")
                completion(false)
            }
        }
    }
}
