import Foundation
import Security
import os

enum UniqueIDError: Error { case keychainWrite, keychainRead }

final class UniqueIDManager {
    static let shared = UniqueIDManager()
    private let account = "internal_user_uuid"
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "uniqueid")

    /// Returns an install-scoped, opaque UUID (v4). Stored only in Keychain.
    func getOrCreateInternalID() throws -> String {
        if let existing = try? readFromKeychain() {
            return existing
        }
        let uuid = UUID().uuidString
        try storeInKeychain(uuid)
        log.info("AUDIT: Internal UUID provisioned") // no PHI
        return uuid
    }

    private func storeInKeychain(_ value: String) throws {
        var cfErr: Unmanaged<CFError>?

        // Strongest practical class for PHI-related secrets on device
        guard let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly,
            [.devicePasscode], // or [.biometryCurrentSet] if you want to tie to biometrics
            &cfErr
        ) else { throw cfErr!.takeRetainedValue() as Error }

        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:               kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String:         account,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String:   ac,
            kSecValueData as String:           Data(value.utf8)
        ]

        let status = SecItemAdd(query as CFDictionary, nil)
        guard status == errSecSuccess else { throw UniqueIDError.keychainWrite }
    }

    private func readFromKeychain() throws -> String {
        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:         kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String:   account,
            kSecReturnData as String:    true
        ]

        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &item)
        guard status == errSecSuccess, let data = item as? Data,
              let str = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) else {
            throw UniqueIDError.keychainRead
        }
        return str
    }
}

import UIKit
import LocalAuthentication
import Security
import os

// MARK: - Session Policy
struct SessionPolicy {
    // Example: 5 minutes inactivity
    static let inactivityTimeout: TimeInterval = 5 * 60
    // Optional absolute lifetime, rolling sessions, etc., can be added
}

// MARK: - Secure Token Store (Keychain)
enum KeychainError: Error { case notFound, writeFailed }

final class SecureTokenStore {
    private let account = "session_token"
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "session")

    func write(token: Data) throws {
        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:                 kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String:           account,
            kSecAttrAccessible as String:        kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
            kSecValueData as String:             token
        ]
        SecItemDelete(query as CFDictionary)
        let status = SecItemAdd(query as CFDictionary, nil)
        guard status == errSecSuccess else {
            log.error("AUDIT: Keychain write failed \(status)")
            throw KeychainError.writeFailed
        }
        log.info("AUDIT: Session token stored securely")
    }

    func read() throws -> Data {
        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:               kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String:         account,
            kSecReturnData as String:          true
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &item)
        guard status == errSecSuccess, let data = item as? Data else {
            throw KeychainError.notFound
        }
        return data
    }

    func delete() {
        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: account
        ]
        SecItemDelete(q as CFDictionary)
        log.notice("AUDIT: Session token deleted")
    }
}

// MARK: - Session Manager (Inactivity + Re-auth)
final class SessionManager {
    static let shared = SessionManager()

    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "session")
    private let tokenStore = SecureTokenStore()

    private var inactivityTimer: Timer?
    private var lastActivity = Date()

    // Notification names for app coordination
    static let sessionExpiredNotification = Notification.Name("SessionExpired")

    // MARK: Public API
    func startSession(with token: Data) {
        try? tokenStore.write(token: token)
        lastActivity = Date()
        scheduleInactivityTimer()
        observeLifecycle()
        log.info("AUDIT: Session started")
    }

    func recordUserActivity() {
        lastActivity = Date()
        resetInactivityTimer()
        log.debug("AUDIT: Activity recorded; timer reset")
    }

    func logout() {
        invalidateSession(reason: "manual_logout")
    }

    // MARK: Timer / Timeout
    private func scheduleInactivityTimer() {
        invalidateTimer()
        inactivityTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1.0, repeats: true) { [weak self] _ in
            self?.tick()
        }
        RunLoop.main.add(inactivityTimer!, forMode: .common)
    }

    private func resetInactivityTimer() { scheduleInactivityTimer() }
    private func invalidateTimer() { inactivityTimer?.invalidate(); inactivityTimer = nil }

    private func tick() {
        let elapsed = Date().timeIntervalSince(lastActivity)
        // pattern: Date().timeIntervalSince(lastActivityDate) > N
        if elapsed > SessionPolicy.inactivityTimeout {
            invalidateSession(reason: "inactivity_timeout")
        }
    }

    // MARK: Invalidate & notify
    private func invalidateSession(reason: String) {
        tokenStore.delete()
        invalidateTimer()
        log.notice("AUDIT: Session invalidated (\(reason))")
        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.sessionExpiredNotification, object: nil)
    }

    // MARK: App lifecycle locks (foreground/ background)
    private func observeLifecycle() {
        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(self,
            selector: #selector(appDidEnterBackground),
            name: UIApplication.didEnterBackgroundNotification, object: nil)

        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(self,
            selector: #selector(appWillEnterForeground),
            name: UIApplication.willEnterForegroundNotification, object: nil)
    }

    @objc private func appDidEnterBackground() {
        // Lock immediately on background
        invalidateSession(reason: "app_backgrounded_lock")
    }

    @objc private func appWillEnterForeground() {
        // Require re-auth on return
        presentReauthenticationIfNeeded()
    }

    // MARK: Re-authentication (biometrics or passcode)
    func presentReauthenticationIfNeeded(completion: ((Bool) -> Void)? = nil) {
        // If there is no token, require login screen
        guard (try? tokenStore.read()) != nil else {
            showLogin()
            completion?(false)
            return
        }

        let ctx = LAContext()
        var error: NSError?
        if ctx.canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication, error: &error) {
            ctx.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication,
                               localizedReason: "Access health records") { [weak self] ok, authError in
                DispatchQueue.main.async {
                    if ok {
                        self?.lastActivity = Date()
                        self?.resetInactivityTimer()
                        self?.log.info("AUDIT: Re-authentication success")
                        completion?(true)
                    } else {
                        self?.log.error("AUDIT: Re-authentication failed: \(authError?.localizedDescription ?? "")")
                        self?.invalidateSession(reason: "reauth_failed")
                        self?.showLogin()
                        completion?(false)
                    }
                }
            }
        } else {
            // Device owner auth unavailable -> force login
            log.error("AUDIT: Device authentication unavailable; redirecting to login")
            invalidateSession(reason: "auth_unavailable")
            showLogin()
            completion?(false)
        }
    }

    private func showLogin() {
        // pattern: presentViewController(AuthViewController.self) or performSegue("showLogin")
        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Notification.Name("ShowLoginUI"), object: nil)
    }
}

// MARK: - Activity Hooks (touches / gestures)
final class ActivityTouchForwarderWindow: UIWindow {
    override func sendEvent(_ event: UIEvent) {
        super.sendEvent(event)
        if event.allTouches?.contains(where: { $0.phase == .began || $0.phase == .moved || $0.phase == .ended }) == true {
            SessionManager.shared.recordUserActivity() // pattern: updateLastActivityTime/resetInactivityTimer
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Example SceneDelegate integration (iOS 13+)
final class SceneDelegate: UIResponder, UIWindowSceneDelegate {
    var window: UIWindow?

    func scene(_ scene: UIScene, willConnectTo session: UISceneSession, options connectionOptions: UIScene.ConnectionOptions) {
        if let ws = scene as? UIWindowScene {
            let w = ActivityTouchForwarderWindow(windowScene: ws)

            self.window = w

            // Navigate to login UI

        }
    }

    func sceneDidBecomeActive(_ scene: UIScene)  { /* pattern match */ }
}

HIPAA rule:
45 CFR §164.312(a) – Access Control
Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain ePHI to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights.
45 CFR §164.312(d) – Person or Entity Authentication
Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
45 CFR §164.312(b) – Audit Controls
Implement mechanisms that record and examine activity in systems containing ePHI (e.g., session expiry, lock/unlock, re-auth events).

HIPAA expectation:
Enforce a session timeout after inactivity and fail closed (invalidate token, clear sensitive state).
On backgrounding or app switch, lock immediately and require re-authentication on return (biometrics or device owner auth).
Track last activity and reset the inactivity timer on user interaction; do not store PHI in UserDefaults.
Keep the session token in Keychain (e.g., kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly) and refuse access when expired/locked.

Secure Unique ID Generation — Spring Implementation

Option 1: UUIDv4 (Random-based, secure default)

import java.util.UUID;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class UniqueIdGenerator {

    public String generateSecureId() {
        // RFC 4122 compliant random UUID
        return UUID.randomUUID().toString();
    }
}

Use this when you need compliance, simplicity, and non-predictability.
Each ID has ~122 bits of randomness — practically collision-free.

Best Practice

  • Use as external identifiers (e.g., patient IDs, request IDs, audit event IDs).

  • Store separately from PHI — never embed PHI in IDs.

  • Use @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.AUTO) internally for DB PKs if needed (internal only).

Option 2: ULID (Lexicographically sortable + Secure random entropy)

import de.huxhorn.sulky.ulid.ULID;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class UlidGenerator {

    private final ULID ulid = new ULID();

    public String generateUlid() {
        // 128-bit ULID (timestamp + randomness)
        return ulid.nextULID();
    }
}

Advantages:

  • Sortable by creation time (helpful for logs)

  • 80 bits randomness, 48 bits timestamp

  • Still non-sequential enough for HIPAA (no patient data leakage)

Option 3: Secure Random Token (HIPAA-grade external references)

For public or external identifiers, use cryptographic random values instead of UUIDs.

import java.security.SecureRandom;
import java.util.Base64;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class SecureTokenGenerator {

    private static final SecureRandom secureRandom = new SecureRandom();

    public String generateToken() {
        byte[] randomBytes = new byte[32]; // 256 bits
        secureRandom.nextBytes(randomBytes);
        return Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(randomBytes);
    }
}

HIPAA benefit:

  • 256-bit entropy ensures unguessable record references.

  • URL-safe Base64 encoding prevents injection risks in APIs.

Use for API tokens, record identifiers in links, or ePHI request tracking IDs.

Integration in JPA Entities (Best Practice)

import jakarta.persistence.*;
import java.util.UUID;

@Entity
@Table(name = "patient_records")
public class PatientRecord {

    @Id
    @Column(length = 36, unique = true, updatable = false, nullable = false)
    private String recordUid = UUID.randomUUID().toString();

    @Column(nullable = false)
    private String name;

    @Version
    private Long version; // Optimistic locking

    // Other fields, getters, setters...
}

References:
  • https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/#jpa.entity-persistence

Force HTTPS & Reject Insecure Requests

Spring Boot Security configuration to enforce HTTPS and redirect insecure HTTP traffic.

import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class NetworkSecurityConfig {

    @Bean
    public SecurityFilterChain securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {

        http
            // 1. Enforce HTTPS
            .requiresChannel(channel -> channel
                .anyRequest().requiresSecure())

            // 2. Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
            .headers(headers -> headers
                .httpStrictTransportSecurity(hsts -> hsts
                    .includeSubDomains(true)
                    .maxAgeInSeconds(31536000))) // 1 year

            // 3. Disable insecure protocols
            .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable()) // use tokens for REST APIs
            .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                .requestMatchers("/health", "/actuator/**").permitAll()
                .anyRequest().authenticated())

            .formLogin().disable()
            .httpBasic().disable();

        return http.build();
    }
}

HIPAA Benefit:

  • Protects ePHI in transit from eavesdropping or MITM.

  • Enforces secure transmission per 164.312(e)(1) & (2)(ii) (“Integrity controls”).


Enforce Strong TLS (Server-side)

For embedded Tomcat / Jetty, enforce TLS 1.2 + only and disable weak ciphers.

# application.yml
server:
  ssl:
    enabled: true
    protocol: TLS
    enabled-protocols: TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3
    ciphers: >
      TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,
      TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,
      TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,
      TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
    key-store: classpath:keystore/secure-keystore.jks
    key-store-password: ${KEYSTORE_PASS}
    key-store-type: JKS

Best Practice:

  • Use a properly signed TLS certificate (CA-issued).

  • Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1.

  • Rotate certificates annually or per policy.

  • Consider FIPS 140-2 validated crypto libraries if required.

Secure HTTP Headers (Defense-in-Depth)

Add standard headers to guard against clickjacking, sniffing, and content injection.

http.headers(headers -> headers
    .xssProtection(xss -> xss.block(true))
    .contentSecurityPolicy(csp -> csp
        .policyDirectives("default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'"))
    .frameOptions(frame -> frame.deny())
    .contentTypeOptions(contentType -> contentType.disable())
    .referrerPolicy(referrer -> referrer.policy(ReferrerPolicyHeaderWriter.ReferrerPolicy.NO_REFERRER))
);

HIPAA Benefit:

  • Ensures integrity of transmitted content.

  • Prevents unauthorized script injection that could leak ePHI.

References:

  • https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/exploits/headers.html#servlet-headers-hsts
  • https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/how-to/webserver.html#howto.webserver.configure-ssl
  • https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/exploits/headers.html

import Foundation
import AuthenticationServices   // ASWebAuthenticationSession
import CryptoKit                // PKCE code verifier/challenge
import Security                 // Keychain
import os

final class OAuthPKCEAuth: NSObject, ASWebAuthenticationPresentationContextProviding {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "oauth")

    // Configure for your IdP
    private let clientID = "<CLIENT_ID>"
    private let authEndpoint = URL(string: "https://idp.example.com/oauth2/v2/auth")!
    private let tokenEndpoint = URL(string: "https://idp.example.com/oauth2/v2/token")!
    private let redirectScheme = "com.example.healthapp"    // CFBundleURLSchemes entry
    private let redirectURI = "com.example.healthapp:/oauth2redirect"

    private var currentSession: ASWebAuthenticationSession?

    // MARK: PKCE
    private func generateVerifierAndChallenge() -> (verifier: String, challenge: String) {
        let verifierData = Data((0..<32).map { _ in UInt8.random(in: 0...255) })
        let verifier = verifierData.base64EncodedString()
            .replacingOccurrences(of: "=", with: "").replacingOccurrences(of: "+", with: "-").replacingOccurrences(of: "/", with: "_")
        let challengeData = Data(SHA256.hash(data: Data(verifier.utf8)))
        let challenge = challengeData.base64EncodedString()
            .replacingOccurrences(of: "=", with: "").replacingOccurrences(of: "+", with: "-").replacingOccurrences(of: "/", with: "_")
        return (verifier, challenge)
    }

    // MARK: Start OAuth (system browser)
    func startLogin(scopes: [String] = ["openid","profile","offline_access"], completion: @escaping (Bool) -> Void) {
        let (verifier, challenge) = generateVerifierAndChallenge()
        let state = UUID().uuidString

        var comps = URLComponents(url: authEndpoint, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)!
        comps.queryItems = [
            .init(name: "client_id", value: clientID),
            .init(name: "response_type", value: "code"),
            .init(name: "redirect_uri", value: redirectURI),
            .init(name: "scope", value: scopes.joined(separator: " ")),
            .init(name: "code_challenge", value: challenge),
            .init(name: "code_challenge_method", value: "S256"),
            .init(name: "state", value: state),
            .init(name: "nonce", value: UUID().uuidString)
        ]

        guard let authURL = comps.url else { completion(false); return }

        let session = ASWebAuthenticationSession(
            url: authURL,
            callbackURLScheme: redirectScheme
        ) { [weak self] callbackURL, error in
            guard error == nil, let url = callbackURL else {
                self?.log.error("AUDIT: OAuth canceled or failed")
                completion(false); return
            }
            // Parse ?code=…&state=…
            guard let qi = URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false)?.queryItems,
                  let code = qi.first(where: { $0.name == "code" })?.value,
                  let returnedState = qi.first(where: { $0.name == "state" })?.value,
                  returnedState == state else {
                self?.log.error("AUDIT: OAuth invalid state or code")
                completion(false); return
            }
            self?.exchangeCodeForTokens(code: code, verifier: verifier, completion: completion)
        }

        session.presentationContextProvider = self
        session.prefersEphemeralWebBrowserSession = true
        currentSession = session
        _ = session.start()
        log.info("AUDIT: OAuth flow started (ASWebAuthenticationSession)")
    }

    // MARK: Token exchange (server)
    private func exchangeCodeForTokens(code: String, verifier: String, completion: @escaping (Bool)->Void) {
        var req = URLRequest(url: tokenEndpoint)
        req.httpMethod = "POST"
        req.setValue("application/x-www-form-urlencoded", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
        let body = [
            "grant_type=authorization_code",
            "code=\(code)",
            "redirect_uri=\(redirectURI)",
            "client_id=\(clientID)",
            "code_verifier=\(verifier)"
        ].joined(separator: "&")
        req.httpBody = body.data(using: .utf8)

        URLSession(configuration: .ephemeral).dataTask(with: req) { data, _, error in
            guard error == nil, let data = data,
                  let json = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String:Any],
                  let access = (json["access_token"] as? String),
                  let refresh = (json["refresh_token"] as? String) else {
                self.log.error("AUDIT: Token exchange failed")
                completion(false); return
            }
            // Store tokens securely (Keychain)
            do {
                try TokenVault.shared.store(accessToken: access, refreshToken: refresh)
                self.log.info("AUDIT: OAuth tokens stored in Keychain")
                completion(true)
            } catch {
                self.log.error("AUDIT: Token vault write failed")
                completion(false)
            }
        }.resume()
    }

    // Presenting context
    func presentationAnchor(for session: ASWebAuthenticationSession) -> ASPresentationAnchor {
        UIApplication.shared.windows.first ?? ASPresentationAnchor()
    }
}

// MARK: Keychain token vault (strong access control)
final class TokenVault {
    static let shared = TokenVault()
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "token")
    private let acctAccess = "oauth_access"
    private let acctRefresh = "oauth_refresh"

    func store(accessToken: String, refreshToken: String) throws {
        try write(key: acctAccess, data: Data(accessToken.utf8))
        try write(key: acctRefresh, data: Data(refreshToken.utf8))
        log.info("AUDIT: Tokens saved (no PHI)")
    }

    func readAccess() throws -> String {
        let d = try read(key: acctAccess); return String(decoding: d, as: UTF8.self)
    }

    private func write(key: String, data: Data) throws {
        var cfErr: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        // Require device passcode or biometry for readout as a second factor when accessing PHI
        guard let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
            [.biometryCurrentSet, .devicePasscode],
            &cfErr
        ) else { throw cfErr!.takeRetainedValue() as Error }

        let q: [String:Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: key,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String: ac,
            kSecValueData as String: data
        ]
        SecItemDelete(q as CFDictionary)
        let st = SecItemAdd(q as CFDictionary, nil)
        guard st == errSecSuccess else { throw NSError(domain: NSOSStatusErrorDomain, code: Int(st)) }
    }

    private func read(key: String) throws -> Data {
        let q: [String:Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
            kSecAttrAccount as String: key,
            kSecReturnData as String: true
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let st = SecItemCopyMatching(q as CFDictionary, &item)
        guard st == errSecSuccess, let data = item as? Data else {
            throw NSError(domain: NSOSStatusErrorDomain, code: Int(st))
        }
        return data
    }
}

2. Social Sign-In routed through OAuth gate: Social SDKs (Google, Facebook, etc.) should not directly grant PHI access. Instead, exchange the provider credential for your backend tokens, then require MFA before issuing an app session.

import GoogleSignIn   // or your chosen provider
import os

final class SocialAuthBridge {

import LocalAuthentication

final class MFAGate {
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "mfa")

HIPAA rule:
45 CFR §164.312(d) – Person or Entity Authentication - Verify that the person/entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
45 CFR §164.312(a) – Access Control - Allow access only to authorized users/programs; enforce least privilege and session controls.
45 CFR §164.312(b) – Audit Controls - Record and examine authentication events (success, failure, MFA, session issue/refresh) without logging PHI.
HIPAA expectation:
OAuth/Social - Use a system browser flow (ASWebAuthenticationSession) or a standards-compliant OAuth client (e.g., AppAuth) with PKCE, state, and nonce. - Never place tokens in UserDefaults or URLs; store only in Keychain with strong access controls.
- After any OAuth/social login, require MFA before issuing an app session that can reach PHI.
MFA
- Enforce a second factor (biometrics or device-owner auth) for PHI access; tie sensitive Keychain entries to biometryCurrentSet or device passcode.
- Handle lockout/cancel securely; fail closed and audit.

import Foundation
import CryptoKit
import Security
import os

enum CryptoErr: Error { case keygen, keyLoad, enc, dec }

final class PHIKeyVault {
    static let shared = PHIKeyVault()
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.healthapp", category: "crypto")
    private let keyAccount = "phi_aes_gcm_key" // 256-bit key

    /// Returns a persistent 32-byte symmetric key from Keychain (creates if absent).
    func symmetricKey() throws -> SymmetricKey {
        if let data = try? readKey() {
            return SymmetricKey(data: data)
        }
        // Generate new 256-bit key
        var keyData = Data(count: 32)
        let rc = keyData.withUnsafeMutableBytes { SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault, 32, $0.baseAddress!) }
        guard rc == errSecSuccess else { throw CryptoErr.keygen }

        // Store with strong access controls (device passcode / biometrics)
        var cfErr: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
            [.biometryCurrentSet, .devicePasscode],
            &cfErr
        )!
        let q: [String:Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:               kSecClassKey,
            kSecAttrApplicationTag as String:  keyAccount,
            kSecAttrKeyType as String:         kSecAttrKeyTypeAES,
            kSecAttrKeySizeInBits as String:   256,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String:   ac,
            kSecValueData as String:           keyData
        ]
        SecItemDelete(q as CFDictionary)
        let st = SecItemAdd(q as CFDictionary, nil)
        guard st == errSecSuccess else { throw CryptoErr.keygen }
        log.info("AUDIT: PHI AES key created & stored (Keychain)")
        return SymmetricKey(data: keyData)
    }

    private func readKey() throws -> Data {
        let q: [String:Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:              kSecClassKey,
            kSecAttrApplicationTag as String: keyAccount,
            kSecReturnData as String:         true
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let st = SecItemCopyMatching(q as CFDictionary, &item)
        guard st == errSecSuccess, let data = item as? Data else { throw CryptoErr.keyLoad }
        return data
    }
}

struct PHICrypto {
    static func encrypt(_ plaintext: Data, using key: SymmetricKey) throws -> Data {
        do {
            let sealed = try AES.GCM.seal(plaintext, using: key)
            // Persist nonce + tag + ciphertext in one blob
            return sealed.combined ?? Data()
        } catch { throw CryptoErr.enc }
    }
    static func decrypt(_ combined: Data, using key: SymmetricKey) throws -> Data {
        do {
            let box = try AES.GCM.SealedBox(combined: combined)
            return try AES.GCM.open(box, using: key)
        } catch { throw CryptoErr.dec }
    }
}

import Foundation

import Security

// MARK: - Logger
let auditLog = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.hipaa", category: "integrity")

// MARK: - Access Control and Keychain Protection
final class PHIKeyManager {
    static let shared = PHIKeyManager()
    private let keyTag = "com.example.hipaa.integrityKey"

    func loadOrCreateIntegrityKey() throws -> SymmetricKey {
        if let existing = try? readKey() { return SymmetricKey(data: existing) }

        var keyData = Data(count: 32)
        _ = keyData.withUnsafeMutableBytes { SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault, 32, $0.baseAddress!) }

        var error: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        let accessControl = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly,
            [.biometryCurrentSet, .userPresence],
            &error
        )!

        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassKey,
            kSecAttrApplicationTag as String: keyTag,
            kSecAttrKeyType as String: kSecAttrKeyTypeAES,
            kSecAttrKeySizeInBits as String: 256,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String: accessControl,
            kSecValueData as String: keyData
        ]
        SecItemDelete(query as CFDictionary)
        SecItemAdd(query as CFDictionary, nil)
        auditLog.notice("AUDIT: Integrity key generated & stored (Keychain, device-only).")
        return SymmetricKey(data: keyData)
    }

    private func readKey() throws -> Data {
        let query: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String: kSecClassKey,
            kSecAttrApplicationTag as String: keyTag,
            kSecReturnData as String: true
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &item)
        guard status == errSecSuccess, let data = item as? Data else {
            throw NSError(domain: "KeyNotFound", code: -1)
        }
        return data
    }
}

// MARK: - Data Integrity (Encryption + Authenticated Tag)

    static func encrypt(_ data: Data) throws -> Data {
        let key = try PHIKeyManager.shared.loadOrCreateIntegrityKey()
        let sealed = try AES.GCM.seal(data, using: key)
        auditLog.notice("AUDIT: PHI encrypted with AES-GCM (integrity tag included).")
        return sealed.combined!
    }

    static func decrypt(_ combined: Data) throws -> Data {
        let key = try PHIKeyManager.shared.loadOrCreateIntegrityKey()
        let box = try AES.GCM.SealedBox(combined: combined)

import Foundation
import Security
import CryptoKit
import os

enum CryptoError: Error { case keyGen, keyLoad, enc, dec, hkdf }

final class KeyVault {
    static let shared = KeyVault()
    private let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app", category: "crypto")
    private let symTag = "com.example.app.phi.symkey"      // kSecAttrApplicationTag
    private let encAttr = kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly

    /// Load/create 256-bit symmetric key (KEK/Data Key) with strong access control.
    func loadOrCreateSymmetricKey() throws -> SymmetricKey {
        if let data = try? readKeyData(tag: symTag) { return SymmetricKey(data: data) }

        var keyData = Data(count: 32)
        let rc = keyData.withUnsafeMutableBytes { SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault, 32, $0.baseAddress!) }
        guard rc == errSecSuccess else { throw CryptoError.keyGen }

        var cfErr: Unmanaged<CFError>?
        let ac = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
            nil,
            encAttr,
            [.biometryCurrentSet, .devicePasscode],
            &cfErr
        )!

        let add: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:               kSecClassKey,
            kSecAttrApplicationTag as String:  symTag,
            kSecAttrKeyType as String:         kSecAttrKeyTypeAES,
            kSecAttrKeySizeInBits as String:   256,
            kSecAttrAccessControl as String:   ac,
            kSecValueData as String:           keyData
        ]
        SecItemDelete(add as CFDictionary)
        let st = SecItemAdd(add as CFDictionary, nil)
        guard st == errSecSuccess else { throw CryptoError.keyGen }
        log.info("AUDIT: Created symmetric key in Keychain (ThisDeviceOnly, biometry/passcode).")
        return SymmetricKey(data: keyData)
    }

    private func readKeyData(tag: String) throws -> Data {
        let q: [String: Any] = [
            kSecClass as String:              kSecClassKey,
            kSecAttrApplicationTag as String: tag,
            kSecReturnData as String:         true
        ]
        var item: CFTypeRef?
        let st = SecItemCopyMatching(q as CFDictionary, &item)
        guard st == errSecSuccess, let data = item as? Data else { throw CryptoError.keyLoad }
        return data
    }
}

2. AES-GCM encryption/decryption (OPTIMAL: CryptoKit AES.GCM with .combined)
import CryptoKit

struct AEAD {
    static func encrypt(_ plaintext: Data) throws -> Data {
        let key = try KeyVault.shared.loadOrCreateSymmetricKey()
        let sealed = try AES.GCM.seal(plaintext, using: key)
        guard let combined = sealed.combined else { throw CryptoError.enc } // nonce|ct|tag
        return combined
    }

    static func decrypt(_ combined: Data) throws -> Data {
        let key = try KeyVault.shared.loadOrCreateSymmetricKey()
        let box = try AES.GCM.SealedBox(combined: combined)
        return try AES.GCM.open(box, using: key)
    }
}

import CryptoKit

struct ECDH {
    /// Generate local Secure Enclave keypair for ECDH.
    static func makeLocalSEKey() throws -> SecureEnclave.P256.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey {
        return try SecureEnclave.P256.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey()
    }

    /// Derive a symmetric session key from ECDH shared secret with HKDF(SHA256).
    static func deriveSessionKey(localPriv: SecureEnclave.P256.KeyAgreement.PrivateKey,
                                 peerPub: P256.KeyAgreement.PublicKey,
                                 salt: Data,
                                 info: Data) throws -> SymmetricKey {
        let shared = try localPriv.sharedSecretFromKeyAgreement(with: peerPub)
        let key = shared.hkdfDerivedSymmetricKey(using: SHA256.self,
                                                 salt: salt,
                                                 sharedInfo: info,
                                                 outputByteCount: 32)
        return key
    }
}

import Foundation
import Security

final class PinnedSessionDelegate: NSObject, URLSessionDelegate {
    func urlSession(_ session: URLSession,
                    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge,
                    completionHandler: @escaping (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) -> Void) {

        guard let trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust else {
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil); return
        }
        // Evaluate trust with system policies (hostname validated by default)
        if SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) {
            completionHandler(.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
        } else {
            completionHandler(.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
        }
    }
}

    let ciphertext = try AEAD.encrypt(plaintext)           // AES-GCM (nonce|ct|tag)

func loadPHIDecrypted(from url: URL) throws -> Data {
    let combined = try Data(contentsOf: url)
    return try AEAD.decrypt(combined)
}

func sendPHISecurely(to endpoint: URL, body: Data) {
    let cfg = URLSessionConfiguration.ephemeral
    let session = URLSession(configuration: cfg, delegate: PinnedSessionDelegate(), delegateQueue: nil)

    var req = URLRequest(url: endpoint)
    req.httpMethod = "POST"
    req.setValue("application/octet-stream", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
    req.httpBody = body  // send AES-GCM ciphertext, never raw PHI

    session.dataTask(with: req).resume()
}

Under HIPAA, authorization ensures that only authorized individuals can access PHI (Protected Health Information) based on defined roles and access levels.
Step 1 — Define Role-Based and Policy-Based Authorization
Use Spring Security’s annotations to control access at the controller and service layers. 
import org.springframework.security.access.prepost.PreAuthorize;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/patient-records")
public class PatientRecordController {

    private final PatientRecordService recordService;

    public PatientRecordController(PatientRecordService recordService) {
        this.recordService = recordService;
    }

    // Only authorized healthcare professionals can view PHI
    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('PHYSICIAN', 'NURSE', 'ADMIN')")
    public ResponseEntity<?> getRecord(@PathVariable Long id) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(recordService.getPatientRecord(id));
    }

    // Only admins can modify or delete PHI
    @DeleteMapping("/{id}")
    @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
    public ResponseEntity<?> deleteRecord(@PathVariable Long id) {
        recordService.deletePatientRecord(id);
        return ResponseEntity.ok("Record securely deleted");
    }
}

Step 2 — Enforce Object-Level Authorization
To comply with HIPAA, authorization shouldn’t stop at endpoints — verify access at the data layer as well.
import org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException;
import org.springframework.security.core.Authentication;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class PatientRecordService {

    private final PatientRecordRepository repository;

    public PatientRecordService(PatientRecordRepository repository) {
        this.repository = repository;
    }

    public PatientRecord getPatientRecord(Long id) {
        Authentication auth = org.springframework.security.core.context.SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
        PatientRecord record = repository.findById(id)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Record not found"));

        // HIPAA-compliant access check: verify user owns the record or has special access
        if (!record.getOwner().equals(auth.getName()) && 
            !auth.getAuthorities().stream().anyMatch(a -> a.getAuthority().equals("ROLE_ADMIN"))) {
            throw new AccessDeniedException("Unauthorized access to patient record");
        }

        return record;
    }
}

Step 3 — Maintain an Authorization Audit Trail
Log every access attempt for compliance and auditing. 
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import org.springframework.security.core.AuthenticationEventPublisher;
import org.springframework.security.authentication.event.*;

@Component
public class AuthorizationAuditLogger implements AuthenticationEventPublisher {

    private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(AuthorizationAuditLogger.class);

    @Override
    public void publishAuthenticationSuccess(AuthenticationSuccessEvent event) {
        logger.info("Authorized access granted to: {}", event.getAuthentication().getName());
    }

    @Override
    public void publishAuthenticationFailure(AuthenticationException exception, Authentication authentication) {
        logger.warn("Unauthorized access attempt by: {}", authentication.getName());
    }
}

Step 4 — Enforce Security at Configuration Level
Ensure endpoint-based protection through Spring Security configuration. 
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.method.configuration.EnableMethodSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;

@EnableMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true)
public class SecurityConfig {

    @Bean
    public SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        http
            .csrf().disable() // For APIs; enable with tokens in UI apps
            .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                .requestMatchers("/api/patient-records/**").authenticated()
                .anyRequest().denyAll()
            )
            .httpBasic(); // or use JWT-based tokens

        return http.build();
    }
}

Setting this to True turns your session into a sliding window on every single request (including background pings), and it forces a DB write per request, which can be noisy/slow at scale. It also makes true inactivity timeouts hard to reason about. Django docs: every request updates the cookie (and expiry) when this is True. 

Better:
Keep SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST = False and implement an explicit idle-timeout middleware that only extends/invalidates on authenticated, meaningful user activity.

Code (middleware core):

# myapp/middleware/inactivity.py
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import logout

IDLE_LIMIT = getattr(settings, "IDLE_LIMIT_SECONDS", 15*60)

class InactivityLogoutMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response): self.get_response = get_response
    def __call__(self, request):
        now = datetime.utcnow().timestamp()
        last = request.session.get("last_activity", now)
        # only consider authenticated, non-static hits
        if request.user.is_authenticated:
            if now - last > IDLE_LIMIT:
                logout(request)                    # server-side invalidate
                request.session.flush()
            else:
                request.session["last_activity"] = now  # extend on *actual* use
        return self.get_response(request)
Why this is better:
Server-enforced idle timeout with explicit tracking is predictable, testable, and avoids hammering the session store on every request. It matches OWASP “idle timeout” guidance without turning on the global “save on every request.”

Resources:
https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/topics/http/sessions/
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/644471/how-do-i-determine-when-a-user-has-an-idle-timeout-in-django

Simply storing last_activity or last_touch in the session without server-side enforcement leaves sessions alive even when the timestamp indicates they should be closed.
Solution:
Adopt a maintained middleware that enforces expiry, or your own minimal middleware that logs out when idle exceeded. Packages like django-session-timeout and django-session-security implement expire-after and warn-before-expire.

Code:
# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS += ["session_security"]           # django-session-security
MIDDLEWARE += ["session_security.middleware.SessionSecurityMiddleware"]
SESSION_SECURITY_EXPIRE_AFTER = 600   # 10 min
SESSION_SECURITY_WARN_AFTER = 540     # 9 min (banner)

Why this is better:
You get enforced idle expiry (and optional warning UI) with fewer foot-guns than hand-rolled flags sprinkled around views.

Step 1 — AEAD at rest (AES-GCM) with centralized crypto service
Store only ciphertext in DB; keys from KMS/secret manager.

# crypto.py
import os, base64
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
class AesGcmService:
    def __init__(self, key: bytes): self.aes = AESGCM(key)
    def encrypt(self, pt: bytes, aad=None) -> str:
        nonce = os.urandom(12); ct = self.aes.encrypt(nonce, pt, aad)
        return base64.b64encode(nonce+ct).decode()
    def decrypt(self, tok: str, aad=None) -> bytes:
        raw = base64.b64decode(tok); return self.aes.decrypt(raw[:12], raw[12:], aad)

# fields.py
from django.db import models
from django.conf import settings
from .crypto import AesGcmService
_aes = AesGcmService(settings.PHI_DEK)
class EncryptedTextField(models.PHI):
    def from_db_value(self, ssn, *a): return None if ssn is None else _aes.decrypt(ssn).decode()
    def get_prep_value(self, ssn):    return None if ssn is None else _aes.encrypt(str(ssn).encode())

To comply with HIPAA’s disposal and media re-use requirements, Laravel applications should ensure that deletion or permanent removal of PHI is authorized, auditable, and irreversible. Only users with specific roles (e.g., Compliance Officer, Data Manager) should be able to perform destruction actions.

1. Authorize destruction requests
Use Laravel’s built-in authorization mechanism to confirm that a user has permission before deleting PHI. When authorization fails, Laravel throws an AuthorizationException or returns an HTTP 403 Forbidden response:
Gate::authorize('delete-patient', $patient);

// or manually
if (! Gate::allows('delete-patient', $patient)) {
    abort(403, 'You are not authorized to delete this record.');
}

2. Implement soft deletes & audit trail
Enable soft deletes to retain a historical record:
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;

class Patient extends Model
{
    use SoftDeletes;
    protected $dates = ['deleted_at'];
}

Record who deleted the data:
$patient->deleted_by = auth()->id();
$patient->save();
$patient->delete();

3. Secure permanent deletion (Disposal)
When retention rules allow, perform secure permanent deletion for both database and file data:
Storage::disk('secure')->delete($path);  // Encrypted disk removal

For local disks, securely wipe files using OS-level commands (shred, srm) inside a queued job.
For cloud storage, configure object lifecycle policies that automatically purge deleted files under controlled IAM roles.

4. Media re-use
Before re-using storage volumes, virtual drives, or staging databases:
  • Overwrite or sanitize media to remove residual ePHI.
  • Rotate encryption keys (php artisan key:generate) to invalidate prior ciphertext.
  • Confirm cleanup of temporary folders (storage/tmp, cache).
  • Restrict re-use operations to authorized system administrators.

5. Log all disposal actions
Create an audit log entry capturing:
  • The user ID performing deletion
  • Time and method of disposal
  • File or record identifiers
  • Verification that no PHI remains

HIPAA requires that any changes to data structures storing ePHI (such as database tables) be authorized, documented, and reversible to ensure data integrity. In Laravel, database migrations provide a structured, version-controlled method for schema management that aligns with these requirements.

1. Create and modify tables through controlled migrations
use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        Schema::create('patients', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->string('name');
            $table->string('email')->unique();
            $table->timestamps();
        });
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        Schema::drop('patients');
    }
};
Using migrations ensures schema changes are traceable and reversible (up() and down() methods).

2. Restrict migration execution permissions
Only authorized system administrators or developers should run migration commands:
php artisan migrate
php artisan migrate:rollback
Restrict production migrations by:
  • Disabling artisan migrate from CI/CD except through approved deployment pipelines.
  • Storing database credentials securely in .env (never in version control).

  • Integrity verification tests post-migration
  • Change approval workflow for destructive operations

Log migration runs (timestamp, user, environment) in a deployment audit log. This ensures accountability if data integrity is compromised by an unauthorized schema alteration.

Database transactions maintain the integrity of electronic protected health information (ePHI) by ensuring that related operations either complete fully or fail entirely. Laravel provides transaction controls to protect against partial or corrupted updates to PHI.

1. Use DB::transaction for atomic operations
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

DB::transaction(function () use ($request) {
    $patient = Patient::findOrFail($request->id);

    $patient->update([
        'name'  => $request->name,
        'email' => $request->email,
    ]);

    Visit::create([
        'patient_id' => $patient->id,
        'notes'      => $request->notes,
    ]);
});
If any exception occurs, Laravel automatically rolls back the transaction to prevent partial updates.

2. Use manual transaction control for complex operations
DB::beginTransaction();

try {
    $patient->update($data);
    $patient->save();

    DB::commit();
} catch (\Throwable $e) {
    DB::rollBack();
    throw $e;
}

3. Combine transactions with validation and authorization
Validate and authorize before committing sensitive data updates:
$this->authorize('update', $patient);
$request->validate(['email' => 'required|email']);

4. Log transaction rollbacks and errors
Record rollback events for integrity monitoring:
Log::error('Transaction failed updating patient', [
    'patient_id' => $patient->id ?? null,
    'user_id'    => auth()->id(),
    'error'      => $e->getMessage(),
]);

5. Keep transactions short
Limit transaction scope to essential write operations to avoid locking and ensure database consistency.

Proper error handling and logging help protect electronic protected health information (ePHI) from improper alteration or destruction by detecting failures, stopping unsafe operations, and recording issues for investigation.

1. Use structured logging for integrity-related events
Log validation failures, database errors, and unexpected exceptions that might impact ePHI:
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;

Log::info('Patient record viewed', [
    'patient_id' => $patient->id,
    'user_id'    => auth()->id(),
]);

Log::warning('Validation failed updating patient', [
    'user_id' => auth()->id(),
    'errors'  => $validator->errors()->all(),
]);

Log::error('Database error updating patient', [
    'patient_id' => $patient->id ?? null,
    'user_id'    => auth()->id(),
    'exception'  => $e->getMessage(),
]);
This supports integrity investigations when something goes wrong with PHI.

2. Validate data before modifying PHI
Use Validator::make or $request->validate() to ensure only valid data updates PHI:
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;

$validator = Validator::make($request->all(), [
    'email' => ['required', 'email'],
    'dob'   => ['required', 'date'],
]);

if ($validator->fails()) {
    Log::warning('Patient update validation failed', [
        'user_id' => auth()->id(),
        'errors'  => $validator->errors()->all(),
    ]);

    return back()->withErrors($validator)->withInput();
}
This prevents malformed or incomplete data from corrupting records.

3. Safely handle database errors (QueryException)
Catch QueryException around critical PHI operations, roll back changes, and log the error:
use Illuminate\Database\QueryException;

try {
    DB::transaction(function () use ($patient, $data) {
        $patient->update($data);
    });
} catch (QueryException $e) {
    Log::error('QueryException during patient update', [
        'patient_id' => $patient->id ?? null,
        'user_id'    => auth()->id(),
        'error'      => $e->getMessage(),
    ]);

    return abort(500, 'An error occurred while processing your request.');
}
This ensures incomplete or broken writes do not remain in the database.

4. Global exception handling for integrity protection
Use Laravel’s exception handler to centralize how unexpected errors are handled:
// app/Exceptions/Handler.php
public function render($request, Throwable $e)
{
    Log::error('Unhandled exception', [
        'user_id' => auth()->id(),
        'error'   => $e->getMessage(),
    ]);

    if ($e instanceof \Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException) {
        return response()->json(['message' => 'Forbidden'], 403);
    }

    return parent::render($request, $e);
}
This prevents sensitive details from leaking while ensuring all serious errors are recorded.

App::abort() (or abort()) should be used to immediately stop potentially unsafe actions:
if ($patient->locked_for_audit) {

        'patient_id' => $patient->id,
        'user_id'    => auth()->id(),

    });
}
You can also create more strict or burst-based policies:
RateLimiter::for('login', function ($request) {
    return [
        Limit::perMinute(5)->by($request->ip()),
    ];
});

2. Apply throttle middleware to routes 
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::middleware(['auth:sanctum', 'throttle:api'])->group(function () {
    Route::get('/patient/{id}', [PatientController::class, 'show']);
});
Or for sensitive endpoints:
Route::post('/login', [AuthController::class, 'login'])
    ->middleware('throttle:login');

3. Handle ThrottleRequestsException gracefully 
use Illuminate\Http\Exceptions\ThrottleRequestsException;

// app/Exceptions/Handler.php
public function render($request, \Throwable $e)
{
    if ($e instanceof ThrottleRequestsException) {
        return response()->json([
            'message' => 'Too many requests. Please try again later.',
        ], 429);
    }

    return parent::render($request, $e);
}
This prevents excessive requests from degrading service for legitimate users and reduces attack surface.

4. Different limits for trusted vs untrusted communication
  • Trusted server-to-server (e.g., internal microservices or VPN-bound IPs): higher limits, IP allowlists, mutual TLS.
  • Public clients: stricter Limit::perMinute() or Limit::perSecond() thresholds, especially on authentication and PHI-related endpoints.

5. Log and monitor throttling events
Log::warning('Rate limit triggered', [
    'ip'      => $request->ip(),
    'user_id' => optional($request->user())->id,
    'route'   => $request->path(),
]);
Repeated throttling from the same IP or token can signal attempted unauthorized access over the network.

API token–based authentication verifies that the caller (user, service, or application) is who it claims to be and helps guard ePHI accessed over HTTP(S) endpoints. In Laravel, the HasApiTokens trait (typically via Sanctum or Passport) enables secure token generation, scoping, and verification.

1. Enable API token authentication on the User model
use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User as Authenticatable;
use Laravel\Sanctum\HasApiTokens;

class User extends Authenticatable
{
    use HasApiTokens;

    // ...
}

2. Issue scoped API tokens for ePHI access 
// In a controller handling login or token creation:
$token = $user->createToken('api-access', ['patients:read', 'patients:update']);

return response()->json([
    'token' => $token->plainTextToken,
]);
Scopes/abilities (like patients:read) limit what each token can do, supporting least-privilege access.

3. Authenticate requests via the Authorization header
Clients send the token with each API call:
GET /api/patients/123
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Laravel Sanctum or Passport validates the token and attaches the authenticated user to the request ($request->user()), ensuring only verified entities access ePHI.

4. Protect routes with auth middleware and ability checks
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::middleware(['auth:sanctum'])->group(function () {
    Route::get('/patients/{patient}', [PatientController::class, 'show'])
        ->middleware('abilities:patients:read');

    Route::put('/patients/{patient}', [PatientController::class, 'update'])
        ->middleware('abilities:patients:update');
});
This ensures only tokens with appropriate abilities can access or modify PHI.

5. Enforce HTTPS for all token-based APIs
  • Serve all API endpoints over HTTPS.
  • Reject or redirect HTTP to HTTPS at the web server level.
  • Never transmit tokens over unencrypted channels.
This supports the transmission security requirement by guarding against interception or unauthorized access while ePHI is in transit.

6. Rotate, expire, and revoke tokens
  • Implement token expiry (short-lived tokens where possible).
  • Revoke tokens when users are deprovisioned or their device is lost:

// Revoke all tokens
$user->tokens()->delete();

// Revoke a specific token
$request->user()->currentAccessToken()->delete();
Regular token hygiene reduces the risk of unauthorized access by stale or compromised tokens.

JWT (JSON Web Token)–based authentication verifies the identity of the caller and protects access to ePHI over APIs. In Laravel, libraries such as tymon/jwt-auth use getJWTIdentifier() on the user model to issue signed tokens that can be validated on each request.

1. Implement JWT on the User model
use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User as Authenticatable;
use Tymon\JWTAuth\Contracts\JWTSubject;

class User extends Authenticatable implements JWTSubject
{
    public function getJWTIdentifier()
    {
        return $this->getKey(); // typically the user primary key
    }

    public function getJWTCustomClaims(): array
    {
        return []; // or include minimal, non-sensitive claims
    }
}
getJWTIdentifier() ties the token to a specific user identity, supporting person/entity authentication.

2. Issue JWTs on successful authentication
use Tymon\JWTAuth\Facades\JWTAuth;

public function login(Request $request)
{
    $credentials = $request->only('email', 'password');

    if (! $token = JWTAuth::attempt($credentials)) {
        return response()->json(['message' => 'Invalid credentials'], 401);
    }

    return response()->json([
        'access_token' => $token,
        'token_type'   => 'bearer',
        'expires_in'   => auth('api')->factory()->getTTL() * 60,
    ]);
}

3. Protect API routes with JWT guard 
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::middleware(['auth:api'])->group(function () {
    Route::get('/patients/{patient}', [PatientController::class, 'show']);
    Route::put('/patients/{patient}', [PatientController::class, 'update']);
});
The auth:api middleware ensures only valid JWTs can access PHI endpoints.

4. Enforce HTTPS for JWT transport
  • Serve all JWT-protected endpoints only over HTTPS.
  • Block or redirect plain HTTP at the web server (Nginx/Apache) layer.
  • Never send JWTs over unencrypted connections or embed them in URLs (query strings).
This aligns with guarding against unauthorized access to ePHI over the network.

5. Token expiration, rotation, and revocation
  • Use short-lived JWTs with refresh tokens where needed.
  • Invalidate tokens on logout or when access is revoked (e.g., using a blacklist or token version column on the user).
  • Regenerate tokens if there is any suspicion of compromise.

6. Limit claims and avoid sensitive data in the token
  • Store only minimal identifiers in JWT claims (e.g., sub as user ID, basic role/ability flags).
  • Do not embed PHI directly in JWT payloads.
  • Rely on server-side lookups for PHI after authenticating the token.
